planner_plan.rationale: The <10 ms end-to-end delay has two stated causes, so the chain pairs one control per cause, both grounded in KPM evidence. Steps 1-2 (kpm observe-rru, observe-ue) capture RRU.PrbTotDl/Ul PRB load and DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, the direct delay KPI; KPM goes first per observation-first routing and satisfies both downstream consumes (slice needs RRU.PrbTotDl, tc needs DRB.RlcSduDelayDl). Step 3 (slice apply-static) applies a STATIC PRB reservation to partition capacity and stop tenant contention on the showroom cells. Step 4 (tc apply-codel) enables CoDel AQM to drain bearer queue build-up and bound bufferbloat. RC is deliberately excluded: its QoS-flow-to-DRB bearer control is explicitly not for slice PRB or queue management, and on this emulator the control is acked with no effect on later KPIs, so it adds latency to the loop without value. Risks: an oversized STATIC reservation could starve best-effort tenants, and CoDel only targets standing queues, so residual jitter may need the fuller tc apply-all profile. RC runs last per rule to push the per-UE radio bearer control and confirm the E2 CONTROL-ACK, matching the operator-accepted [KPM, SLICE, TC, RC] chain for the near-identical 'XR latency below 5 ms' intent; 4 steps stays within the 1–4 preference and all consumes (RRU.PrbTotDl, DRB.RlcSduDelayDl) are produced by the earlier KPM step. Risks: on the FlexRIC emulator the RC control is acknowledged but has no effect on later KPIs, so rc-control validates delivery only, not delay improvement; slice.apply-static reserves capacity but cannot fix residual bufferbloat, and tc.apply-codel cannot fix radio-side contention — both legs are needed. Next best action: run this chain, then re-check DRB.RlcSduDelayDl and RRU.PrbTotDl via a follow-up KPM observation to verify end-to-end delay stays under 10 ms and re-tune the slice PRB reservation if contention persists.

planner_plan.rationale: Venue-full contention plus a hard RTT/jitter SLA calls for observe-then-control. KPM (observe-rru) runs first to capture PRB utilisation and RLC SDU delay evidence before any decision. Slice (apply-static) then reserves PRBs for the gaming tenant so competing tenants cannot starve the shared cells - directly required by the 'venue full, other tenants compete' condition; its consume RRU.PrbTotDl is provided by the earlier KPM step. TC (apply-codel) next caps queueing delay and jitter on the bearer path, the core levers for the 20 ms RTT / 5 ms jitter targets; its consume DRB.RlcSduDelayDl is provided by KPM. RC (rc-control) finishes last, mapping the gaming tenant's QoS flow to a dedicated DRB and confirming the E2 CONTROL-ACK, per the rule that RC applies/validates control at the end. This mirrors the operator-accepted chain for the prior 'XR latency below 5 ms' intent ([KPM, SLICE, TC, RC]); unlike the rejected investigation intents, active writers are required here because the intent demands an enforced guarantee, not diagnosis. Risks: on the FlexRIC emulator the RC control is acknowledged but has no effect on later KPIs, so RC serves as actuation/confirmation only; an oversized STATIC reservation could starve best-effort tenants. Next best action: execute the chain, then re-read KPM delay/PRB KPIs against the 20 ms RTT and 5 ms jitter targets and re-tune the slice/TC profiles if either is breached.

planner_plan.rationale: Deadline misses appear only when camera-inspection uploads start, indicating shared-resource contention, so KPM observe-rru runs first to capture PRB utilisation (UL for camera uplink, DL for AGV traffic) and RLC SDU delay as baseline contention evidence. Slice apply-static then reserves PRBs (STATIC profile) to isolate the AGV control slice from camera-inspection load — the radio-resource fix. TC apply-all applies CoDel AQM with shaping and traffic classification on the bearer path plus the RLC monitor, attacking bufferbloat-induced queueing delay and returning RLC.queue_stats to confirm the queueing fix. RC rc-control finishes the chain by pushing the QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping for the AGV bearer and confirming the E2 CONTROL-ACK, validating the applied control decision. Dependencies hold: slice consumes RRU.PrbTotDl and tc consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, both produced by the earlier KPM step; rc has no prerequisites and is placed last per policy. This matches the operator-accepted pattern for similar latency-under-load intents (KPM, SLICE, TC, RC). Risks: on this emulator the RC control is acknowledged but has no effect on later KPIs, and the 4-step cap leaves no room for a post-change measurement pass — run a follow-up kpm observe-ue after the chain to verify the 10 ms AGV cycle deadline is recovered before closing the loop.

Risks: two-hour duration requires periodic re-evaluation rather than one-shot enforcement; if slice policy alone cannot hold 15 Mbit/s, escalation to admission control may be needed. Next best action: run the chain, then loop KPM->SLICE/TC on a short interval for the session's full duration, alerting if delay approaches the 50 ms budget.

planner_plan.rationale: Novel 4-step chain; no template reused unchanged because observe-diagnose-optimize uses slice 'monitor' (read-only), which cannot reserve PRB capacity against co-tenant load on the clinic cell. (1) kpm/observe-rru first per observation rule: baseline RRU.PrbTotDl/Ul, DRB.UEThpDl and DRB.RlcSduDelayDl before any control. (2) slice/apply-static applies a STATIC PRB reservation so other tenants sharing the cell cannot starve the 15 Mbit/s video rate; its consumes (RRU.PrbTotDl) is satisfied by step 1. (3) tc/apply-all runs the full transport profile (CoDel AQM plus classification/partitioning) with the RLC monitor on the shared transport link to hold queueing delay under the 50 ms budget; consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl from step 1. (4) rc/rc-control last per control rule: maps the ultrasound QoS flow (QFI 10) to DRB 5 DL and validates via E2 CONTROL-ACK. Risks: on this emulator RC control is ACKed but does not affect later KPIs; rc-control is fixed to amf_ue_ngap_id 1 / DRB 5 / QFI 10, so confirm it matches the ultrasound UE; DRB.RlcSduDelayDl is a radio-side proxy, not full end-to-end one-way delay; the STATIC reservation reduces capacity left for best-effort tenants. Next best action: execute the chain, then re-run kpm after ~15 minutes to confirm DRB.UEThpDl >= 15 Mbit/s and DRB.RlcSduDelayDl within budget, and schedule periodic re-checks for the remainder of the 2-hour session.

planner_plan.rationale: Evening video lag while bulk downloads saturate sector 12 indicates bufferbloat plus radio capacity contention, so the chain is composed rather than reusing a template. Step 1 kpm/observe-ue gathers the evidence base (DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, DRB.UEThpDl, plus RRU.PrbTotDl in the kpm.snapshot) and satisfies the consumes of both downstream control agents. Step 2 tc/apply-codel directly targets the queueing delay hurting video calls (AQM/shaping on the bearer path; consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl from kpm). Step 3 slice/apply-static partitions PRB per slice so bulk traffic cannot starve video flows at evening peak (consumes RRU.PrbTotDl from kpm). Step 4 rc/rc-control applies the per-UE QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping for video bearers and validates via E2 CONTROL-ACK, per the rule that RC acts last. Risks: on the FlexRIC emulator the RC control is acknowledged but has no effect on later KPIs, and TC/slice gains are not verified within this 4-step budget. Next best action: after the chain completes, run a follow-up kpm/observe-ue window to confirm RLC SDU delay and video throughput improvement during the evening peak, and re-trigger tc/slice if delay remains elevated.

planner_plan.rationale: Observation: evening FWA pattern indicates bulk downloads saturate sector 12 PRB, inflating bearer queues so latency-sensitive video calls suffer bufferbloat lag. Plan: KPM first for congestion evidence (RRU.PrbTotDl, plus DRB.UEThpDl/DRB.RlcSduDelayDl via the shared bus), which satisfies slice's consumed RRU.PrbTotDl and TC's consumed DRB.RlcSduDelayDl. Slice apply-static (not monitor) enforces a STATIC PRB reservation so bulk traffic cannot crowd out interactive video - the intent demands remediation, not read-only observation. TC apply-codel then mitigates queueing delay/bufferbloat on the bearer path, the direct fix for video lag; TC is mandatory per operator history (proposals missing TC were rejected). RC is last per policy: push the QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping (QFI 10 to DRB 5) for the video bearer and confirm the E2 CONTROL-ACK. Risks: on the FlexRIC emulator RC control is acknowledged but has no effect on later KPIs, so treat RC as procedural validation only; the STATIC slice profile is fixed-configuration; load is diurnal so results must be checked in the same evening window. Next best action: re-run KPM observe-ue during the next evening peak to confirm DRB.RlcSduDelayDl drops and video throughput recovers; if video UEs still lag, follow up with a dedicated video slice profile or per-UE treatment.

This mirrors the operator-accepted [KPM, SLICE, TC, RC] pattern for latency-guarantee intents while swapping slice monitor->apply-static because correction, not just monitoring, is required. Risks: a static PRB reservation may waste capacity off-peak and needs retuning; CoDel is transport-level, so if uplink PRB stays saturated the slice split must be enlarged. Step 3 tc/apply-all runs CoDel AQM plus classification/RLC monitor on the bearer path to drain the bloated queues and cut DRB.RlcSduDelayDl for snappy page loads; its consumes (DRB.RlcSduDelayDl) is satisfied by step 1. Step 4 kpm/observe-ue closes the loop by re-measuring UE KPIs to confirm median throughput >20 Mbit/s and low RLC SDU delay. RC is deliberately excluded: its QoS-flow-to-DRB control is out of scope for slice PRB partitioning and queue management (per its own card), and on this emulator the control is ACKed but has no KPI effect, so it cannot serve the goal or validation. Risks: a STATIC reservation sized only on the evening baseline may starve a bursty slice at other hours; TC shaping trades a small amount of deliberate latency; if step 4 still shows median <20 Mbit/s the reservation likely needs re-partitioning. planner_plan.rationale: Observations: the 19:00-23:00 degradation has two stated root causes - inter-slice PRB contention and bufferbloat on shared bearer queues - so the chain must both partition radio resources and fix queueing. kpm runs first (observe-rru) to baseline RRU.PrbTotDl/PrbTotUl plus the DRB.UEThpDl and DRB.RlcSduDelayDl evidence needed downstream. slice (apply-static) then enforces the STATIC profile to reserve PRBs per slice and stop the contention; its consume RRU.PrbTotDl is satisfied by the kpm step. tc (apply-codel) applies CoDel AQM to drain the bloated queues and cut RLC SDU delay for snappy page loads; its consume DRB.RlcSduDelayDl is satisfied by kpm. rc (rc-control) is placed last per policy to actuate and validate the control path via E2 CONTROL-ACK. Risks: the RC card notes the emulator acknowledges control without affecting later KPIs, so the throughput gain must come from the slice+TC controls; STATIC reservations must be sized from the kpm baseline or one slice may starve; and the 4-step cap with RC-last leaves no in-chain post-control KPI check. planner_plan.rationale: Evening DL collapse has two named root causes — slices fighting over PRBs and bloated shared bearer queues — so the chain observes, partitions, then de-bloats. (1) kpm observe-rru first, per the KPM-first rule, capturing RRU.PrbTotDl, DRB.UEThpDl and DRB.RlcSduDelayDl evidence; this satisfies downstream consumes (slice needs RRU.PrbTotDl, tc needs DRB.RlcSduDelayDl). (2) slice apply-static instead of monitor: the intent demands per-slice PRB partitioning to stop contention and lift median DL throughput above 20 Mbit/s, which read-only monitoring cannot deliver. (3) tc apply-codel applies CoDel AQM on the bearer path to drain bufferbloat and restore snappy page loads. (4) rc rc-control last, per the RC-last rule, closing the loop with an E2SM-RC CONTROL plus CONTROL-ACK validation. This mirrors the operator-accepted [KPM, SLICE, TC, RC] chain for downlink congestion; prior proposals omitting SLICE were rejected, so SLICE is retained. Risks: on the FlexRIC emulator the RC control is ACKed but does not move later KPIs, so treat the ACK as confirmation of control delivery only; next best action after execution is a follow-up kpm observation in the 19:00-23:00 window to verify median DRB.UEThpDl > 20 Mbit/s and reduced DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, re-running slice/tc adjustments if the target is missed.

planner_plan.rationale: The intent spans three coupled objectives: protect 400 concurrent lecture streams, cap research transfer queue inflation, and avoid starving the research slice. KPM first establishes per-UE/per-slice KPIs (buffer occupancy, BLER, throughput) to quantify MAC pressure from the mass streaming load. SLICE then enforces slice-level policy so research transfers stay within their slice allocation rather than competing with lecture traffic. TC applies queue/traffic controls to stop large dataset transfers from inflating shared queues. RC validates the resulting policy state and confirms control actions took effect. The alternatives are insufficient: slice-assurance lacks TC queue enforcement against transfer-induced queue buildup, and transport-qos is TC-only with no slice policy or validation loop.

KPM runs first to supply the required evidence: it produces RRU.PrbTotDl (consumed by slice) and DRB.RlcSduDelayDl (consumed by tc), satisfying all consumes constraints. slice/apply-static then partitions PRBs per slice, isolating the lecture slice from the research transfers while reserving a capacity floor so the research slice is not starved. tc/apply-all finishes with CoDel/ECN AQM plus classification and shaping (RLC monitor included), so large dataset transfers cannot inflate everyone's queues and streaming queueing delay stays low. Risks: STATIC profile defaults may be mis-sized for a 400-UE lecture hall and may need retuning; tc classification must distinguish lecture streaming from bulk transfer classes. planner_plan.rationale: Verification-only intent (confirm 20% PRB reservation in force and that tenant users realize its capacity), so no control actuation is planned. Step 1 (kpm/observe-rru) satisfies the KPM-first rule for observation and yields the RRU.PrbTotDl baseline that the slice agent consumes. Step 2 (slice/monitor, read-only) reads current slice state over E2SM-SLICE to confirm the STATIC 20% PRB reservation is actually applied and reports UE-to-slice associations and reserved capacity. Step 3 (kpm/observe-ue) reads DRB.UEThpDl and per-UE PRB/throughput to verify tenant users get the capacity the reservation should provide, closing the assurance loop. RC is excluded: no control decision is being applied or validated, the RC card explicitly forbids slice PRB reservation use, and its control is acknowledged but has no KPI effect on this emulator. TC is excluded: no transport/queue symptoms in the intent. All dependencies hold (slice consumes RRU.PrbTotDl produced by step 1); 3 steps within the 1-4 preference; no deprecated cards used. Risks: slice monitor may show the reservation absent or drifted (onboarding misconfiguration), and UE throughput may lag reservation state if tenant traffic is light. Next best action if step 2 shows the reservation not in force: re-run with slice/apply-static to enforce the 20% STATIC profile, then repeat kpm/observe-ue to validate impact.

Next best action: run the chain during a representative load window and compare slice-reported reserved PRBs against per-UE DRB.UEThpDl; escalate to a slice reconfiguration only if the monitor step shows the policy not in force.

planner_plan.rationale: Read-only RAN-sharing audit, so no control actuation is warranted and RC is omitted (its emulator control is acknowledged but has no KPI effect). Step 1 (kpm/observe-rru) establishes carrier-wide PRB utilisation (RRU.PrbTotDl) and satisfies the slice agent's consumed input. Step 2 (slice/monitor) reads, without control, the reserved per-slice capacity and UE-to-slice associations to verify operator B's 30% STATIC reservation is actually configured and enforced. Step 3 (kpm/observe-ue) samples per-UE/DRB throughput (DRB.UEThpDl) and RLC delay for operator B's associated UEs to compare achieved share against the 30% entitlement. Risk: on the FlexRIC emulator KPIs may be synthetic and slice reservations are STATIC-only, so a mismatch indicates configuration drift rather than scheduler dynamics; if a shortfall is confirmed, the next best action is a separate change-window chain (kpm -> slice/apply-static -> kpm -> rc) to re-assert the partition and validate.

planner_plan.rationale: Observations: CHG-2231 requires (1) enacting the STATIC slice profile and (2) quantifying per-slice load impact, so the chain is a baseline-measure -> actuate -> re-measure loop. Step 1 (kpm/observe-rru) captures pre-change PRB utilisation as the per-slice load baseline; KPM leads per policy since the task is measurement-driven. Step 2 (slice/apply-static) puts the CHG-2231 STATIC profile into effect on the test cell; its consumes (RRU.PrbTotDl) is satisfied by step 1, and the action's built-in monitor returns UE-to-slice associations and reserved capacity. Step 3 (kpm/observe-rru) repeats the RRU observation post-change so the per-slice load delta can be diffed against the baseline for sign-off. RC is excluded: slice PRB reservation is explicitly out of RC scope (radio bearer control only, and its emulator ACK does not affect KPIs); TC is excluded as there is no transport/queue intent. Risks: keep baseline and post-change KPM windows equal in length and load conditions, or the delta is not attributable to CHG-2231; on the emulator, control effects may be limited, so validate via slice.ue_association and reserved-capacity reporting as well as KPM. Next best action: execute the chain, diff RRU.PrbTotDl/RRU.PrbTotUl per slice between steps 1 and 3, and attach the delta to CHG-2231 for approval.

planner_plan.rationale: Post-migration intent is a read-only compliance check, so no template is forced and no control is applied. Step 1 (kpm/observe-rru) collects current PRB usage evidence (RRU.PrbTotDl) and satisfies the slice card's consumes, which the rules require to come from an earlier step; KPM-first also matches the observation/diagnosis rule. Step 2 (slice/monitor) reads UE-to-slice associations to confirm every sensor UE landed in the mMTC slice (not the default) and reads reserved capacity to verify PRB usage stays inside the reservation. RC is omitted: no control decision is applied or validated here, rc-control pushes an unrelated bearer config (DRB 5/QFI 10) that is acknowledged but has no KPI effect on the emulator, and rc-report RRC state does not indicate slice membership. TC is irrelevant (transport/queue scope). This intentionally reorders the previously accepted ['SLICE','KPM','RC'] audit chain because the current consumes rule forbids slice-first (it consumes RRU.PrbTotDl) and the RC tail adds no value for verification-only. Risks: a short KPM window may miss steady-state post-migration PRB load, and if the monitor finds sensor UEs in the default slice or a PRB overage, remediation is out of scope for this run. Next best action: execute the chain; on violation, re-plan a corrective run with slice/apply-static (with RC appended last only if a control decision is then pushed and needs ack validation).

planner_plan.rationale: Post-upgrade verification is read-only diagnosis, so KPM leads per the observation-first rule. Step 1 (observe-rru) captures PRB utilisation and produces RRU.PrbTotDl, satisfying the slice agent's consumes requirement; step 2 (observe-ue) adds UE throughput (DRB.UEThpDl) and RLC SDU delay as the traffic-level evidence. Step 3 runs slice in monitor mode (read-only, no control) to read the current slice policy, reserved capacity and UE-to-slice associations, confirming the slice configuration survived the gNB upgrade; correlating slice.ue_association with DRB.UEThpDl validates that per-slice traffic levels look normal. No control decision is applied or validated, so RC is excluded (its bearer control is unrelated and acknowledged-but-ineffective on the emulator), TC is out of scope, and slice apply-static is deliberately avoided so the verification cannot alter the configuration being checked. All cards are status ready; none deprecated. Risk: this chain detects but cannot remediate - if PRB/throughput or slice associations look wrong after the upgrade, the next best action is a follow-up chain ending in slice apply-static to restore the intended slice policy. 3 steps, within the 1-4 preference.

KPM runs first per the observation rule, capturing PRB utilisation and throughput to judge whether slice traffic levels look normal after the upgrade; this also satisfies the slice agent's consumes dependency on RRU.PrbTotDl. Slice monitor then reads UE-to-slice associations and reserved capacity to confirm the slice configuration survived the gNB software upgrade without pushing any control. RC is omitted because no control decision is applied or validated (its bearer control is unrelated to slice config and acknowledged-only on the emulator); TC is irrelevant to slice assurance. Risk: the KPM window is short, so a transient traffic dip right after the upgrade could look anomalous; if KPIs or slice associations look wrong, the next best action is a longer KPM observation window and, only with operator approval, slice apply-static to restore the intended STATIC profile.

planner_plan.rationale: The intent is a read-only review of slice PRB quotas versus measured usage, so no control actuation is warranted and RC is omitted (its control scope is per-UE bearer mapping, not slice PRB). KPM runs first to satisfy the observation rule and to produce RRU.PrbTotDl, which the slice agent consumes; observe-rru targets the PRB-utilisation records needed for cell 3. Slice then runs its monitor action, which is explicitly the read-only path for current slice state, reserved PRB capacity, and UE-to-slice associations, enabling a direct quota-vs-usage comparison. Step 1 (kpm/observe-rru) collects current RRU PRB utilisation from the KPM bus and produces RRU.PrbTotDl, which satisfies the slice agent's consumes requirement. Next best action: if the review shows reservation/usage drift on cell 3, run a follow-up chain slice/apply-static then kpm/observe-rru to enforce and re-measure.

planner_plan.rationale: The intent is a dedicated transport queue partition with traffic classification so IoT telemetry stops queuing behind video segments; only the TC agent provides this (transport_qos, bufferbloat_mitigation, traffic_shaping). TC consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, so KPM must run first (observe-ue reads DRB-oriented KPM records) to supply baseline delay evidence. TC apply-all is chosen over apply-codel because the full profile includes partitioning and classification plus the RLC monitor, whereas CoDel alone is only AQM. A final KPM observe-ue verifies the telemetry bearer's RLC SDU delay improved, closing the loop. RC is excluded: its card explicitly forbids queue management and its E2SM-RC control is ack-only with no effect on later KPIs on the emulator. Slice is excluded: PRB reservation is radio-resource partitioning, not a transport queue partition, and its card forbids transport/queue policies. Risk: on the FlexRIC emulator, confirm the TC policy actually took effect via the RLC monitor output; if telemetry delay does not improve after apply-all, the next best action is a follow-up slice-level PRB partition (slice apply-static) as a complementary isolation measure.

planner_plan.rationale: Observations: The intent is per-class transport queue treatment (dedicated partition for IoT telemetry behind video segments), which maps to the TC service model (queue partitioning, traffic classification). No operator template matches: 'transport-qos' is TC-only and would violate the consumes rule since TC requires DRB.RlcSduDelayDl from an earlier step, so a novel 2-step chain is composed. KPM runs first to baseline DRB-level queueing delay (observe-ue targets UE/DRB KPIs) and satisfies TC's consumes dependency. TC apply-all is chosen over apply-codel because the full profile includes classification/partitioning plus the RLC monitor, which produces RLC.queue_stats for immediate post-change validation and closes the loop without an extra step. RC is deliberately excluded: its card forbids queue management use, its QoS-flow-to-DRB control is a different mechanism, and on this emulator the control is acked but has no effect on later KPIs, so it would add latency without validation value. Slice is excluded: its card forbids transport/queue policies and PRB reservation does not create queue partitions. Risks: TC policy applies to the whole bearer path, so misclassification could over-throttle video or starve other classes; validation here relies on RLC.queue_stats and KPM deltas rather than an RC control-ack; emulator TC effects may be simulated rather than reflected in real queueing. Next best action: execute kpm(observe-ue) -> tc(apply-all), then re-run kpm observe-ue and compare DRB.RlcSduDelayDl for IoT flows against the baseline; if the partition does not reduce IoT queueing delay, revisit TC classification weights before considering slice-level isolation.

planner_plan.rationale: A standing ~300 ms queue on the bearer is a bufferbloat problem, so the chain is observe -> actuate -> verify. Step 1 (kpm/observe-ue) baselines the queue and supplies DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, the only data the TC agent consumes. Step 2 (tc/apply-codel) applies CoDel, the active queue discipline matched to draining a standing queue; TC is the only ready card covering transport AQM/bufferbloat mitigation. Step 3 (kpm/observe-ue) re-reads DRB.RlcSduDelayDl to confirm the queue drained toward CoDel's ~5 ms target. RC is excluded: its card explicitly forbids queue management, its E2SM-RC control (QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping) is ack-only with no effect on later KPIs on the emulator, and the rule to place RC last applies only when an RC control decision is in scope. Slice is excluded because no PRB partitioning or slice isolation is requested. Risk: if post-control delay remains ~300 ms, escalate to tc/apply-all (full profile with shaping and RLC monitor) rather than introducing RC or slice controls.

rationale.next_best_action: Execute kpm(observe-ue) -> tc(apply-all), then re-run kpm observe-ue to compare DRB.RlcSduDelayDl pre/post and confirm gaming-class queue delay drops; if per-slice PRB isolation is later required, extend with the slice agent.
rationale.observations: Intent is per-class transport-queue treatment (strict priority for low-latency gaming, best-effort deprioritized), so TC is the only valid executor: it owns traffic classification, partitioning and queue management. RC is explicitly excluded for queue management and its control is ack-only with no KPI effect on the emulator; SLICE is PRB partitioning, not transport queues. KPM must precede TC because TC consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, which only KPM produces; observe-ue reads the DRB-oriented records that carry it. apply-all is chosen over apply-codel because the full profile includes partitioning and traffic classification needed for class-based strict priority, whereas CoDel alone is class-agnostic AQM. The transport-qos template was not reused verbatim: its single TC step leaves TC's consumes unsatisfied and its CoDel profile cannot express strict priority.
rationale.risks: Strict priority can starve best-effort if no shaper backs it; verify via post-check. On the FlexRIC emulator, TC effects may only surface in RLC.queue_stats/RLC delay rather than end-to-end KPIs. No RC confirmation step is possible/appropriate here, so validation must be measurement-based.

planner_plan.rationale: Diagnose-then-actuate closed loop. Step 1 (kpm/observe-ue) samples DRB.RlcSduDelayDl and DRB.UEThpDl during the rush-hour window to confirm or refute queueing delay as the choppy-voice cause. Step 2 (tc/apply-all) is the only transport-path actuator: traffic classification prioritises conversational voice per-class on the bearer path while CoDel AQM drains bufferbloat; it consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl produced by step 1, and its built-in RLC monitor yields immediate queue stats. Step 3 repeats kpm/observe-ue as the post-control measurement check to verify delay/jitter reduction. Slice agent is excluded: the slice plan is frozen this week and PRB partitioning is out of scope. RC is excluded: the intent is transport-path prioritisation (TC scope), RC's card forbids queue-management use, and on this emulator its control is ack-only with no KPI effect, so appending it would add handoff latency without validation value. Risks: if step 1 shows delay flat but RRU.PrbTotDl saturated, the bottleneck is radio-side, not transport — abort before step 2 and re-plan; TC policy takes effect at ~1 s timescale, so allow a comparable rush-hour window before judging step 3. Next best action: run the chain, gate step 2 on a confirmed DRB.RlcSduDelayDl elevation, and compare step 3 vs step 1 delay distributions for the voice class.

planner_plan.rationale: Diagnosis before control: KPM observe-ue reads UE/DRB-oriented KPM records and surfaces DRB.RlcSduDelayDl (the queueing-delay evidence needed to confirm or rule out rush-hour bufferbloat) plus DRB.UEThpDl. TC apply-all then consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl (dependency satisfied by the earlier KPM step) and runs the full profile: CoDel AQM to cut queueing delay plus traffic classification/partitioning to prioritise conversational voice on the transport path, with the bundled RLC monitor (RLC.queue_stats) validating post-change queue behaviour. Slice is excluded: the slice plan is frozen this week and operator history rejects SLICE as a forbidden writer when slice changes are not required. RC is excluded: the actuation is transport-side (TC domain), not per-UE radio bearer control — RC's card forbids its use for queue management, and on the emulator its CONTROL-ACK has no effect on later KPIs. This is a novel 2-step chain: the transport-qos template lacks the required diagnosis step, and observe-diagnose-optimize pulls in the frozen SLICE writer and an unnecessary RC control. Risk/gating: step 2 should only execute if KPM confirms elevated DRB.RlcSduDelayDl; if delay is low, stop after observation and investigate radio-side causes instead. Next best action: run the chain, then re-run KPM observe-ue after the TC policy settles to confirm queueing-delay reduction.

The KPM agent is read-only and directly produces both required metrics, so it is selected first and only, using observe-rru for cell-level PRB/load context on the two cells and observe-ue for the per-UE throughput and RLC SDU delay evidence. No control agents (rc, tc, slice) are included: rc-control, TC AQM/shaping, and slice apply-static would all mutate RAN state, violating the no-change constraint, and rc is only to be used last when a control decision is actually applied. If the KPI review later concludes control is warranted, a follow-up chain (e.g., kpm -> tc apply-codel for delay, or kpm -> rc for per-UE bearer control) can be planned then; kpm's outputs already satisfy those agents' consumes requirements.

Next best action: run kpm/observe-ue scoped to the two campus cells and attach the snapshot to the dispute ticket for the control-warranted review.

planner_plan.rationale: Read-only triage: the intent forbids any configuration change, so all write-capable actions (tc apply-codel/apply-all, slice apply-static, rc rc-control) are excluded, and no operator template is reused since every matching template embeds writers. KPM leads per the observation rule. Step 1 (observe-rru) samples cell-level RRU.PrbTotDl/Ul to test cell-wide congestion; step 2 (observe-ue) samples per-UE DRB.RlcSduDelayDl and DRB.UEThpDl to place the outlier UE against the cell median. Attribution rule: high cell PRB utilisation with broadly elevated delay => cell at fault; near-normal cell PRB with one UE showing ~10x delay and depressed throughput => the UE's own radio link. Risks: KPM is read-only so no remediation occurs, and short observation windows can miss bursty congestion — widen the window or re-run before concluding. Next best action: report the attribution to the operator, then stage any control chain (RC bearer control for a UE-link fault, TC/slice for cell or transport pressure) as a separate, explicitly approved run.

planner_plan.rationale: Observation: single-UE RLC delay outlier (10x cell median) in the hospital cell; intent is diagnosis only, so every write scope is forbidden and no operator template is reused (all three end in a TC/SLICE/RC control action). KPM leads per the triage rule. Step 1 (observe-rru) collects cell-level RRU.PrbTotDl to test the cell-congestion hypothesis; step 2 (observe-ue) collects per-UE DRB.RlcSduDelayDl and DRB.UEThpDl to compare the outlier against the cell median and peers. Verdict logic: high cell PRB utilisation with broadly elevated delay => cell at fault; normal cell PRB with isolated low UE throughput plus high RLC SDU delay => the UE's own radio link. Exclusions: TC (only actions are writers apply-codel/apply-all; matches past rejection 'TC: forbidden writer'), slice apply-static and rc-control (writers), rc-report (RRC state only, no RLC attribution value). Risks: KPI correlation is indicative rather than conclusive, and a short KPM window can miss bursty congestion; no remediation is possible within this read-only chain. Next best action: run the two KPM passes, then branch - if the cell is at fault, plan a KPM->SLICE/TC->RC remediation loop; if the UE link is at fault, plan per-UE RC bearer control followed by a KPM post-check.

No operator template matches an alarm-verification intent, so a novel read-only chain is composed. Step 1 (kpm/observe-rru) re-reads RRU.PrbTotDl/PrbTotUl on cell 9 to confirm or refute the 90% reading at the source. Step 2 (kpm/observe-ue) cross-checks DRB.UEThpDl and RLC delay: sustained high PRB with proportionate UE throughput indicates genuine load, while high PRB with flat or absent throughput points to a counter glitch. KPM is correctly first (observation rule), requires nothing, and both steps are read-only so dependency and safety constraints hold. Risks: a single short KPM window may miss intermittent glitches; emulator KPIs may not reflect real cell 9 state. Next best action: if both observations corroborate sustained high PRB with real throughput, escalate to a mitigation workflow (e.g., slice/TC writers) under a separate actuation intent; if they diverge, flag the KPM subscription/counter as suspect and re-subscribe before alarming again.

KPM runs first (rule: KPM first for diagnosis/anomaly evidence): observe-rru captures PRB utilisation to detect an overnight load/congestion shift, and observe-ue captures DRB.UEThpDl and DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, the direct evidence of user-visible sluggishness. TC is excluded because its only actions (apply-codel, apply-all) write transport policy, violating the no-act constraint. RC is excluded because no control decision is being applied or validated, and rc-report (RRC state) adds little beyond KPM for this symptom. Risks: the KPM window is short, so an overnight change may need a longer baseline comparison; slice monitor is read-only, so no remediation occurs in this run. Next best action: if KPM shows sustained PRB saturation or rising RLC delay, escalate to an approved remediation chain (tc apply-codel for bufferbloat/delay, or slice apply-static for capacity repartitioning) with a post-control KPM validation step.

planner_plan.rationale: Observation: intent needs measurement confirmation of the sub-50 Mbit/s DL throughput breach on the mission-critical slice, then an enlarged radio (PRB) reservation, with transport queues untouched. Chain: kpm observe-rru first (KPM-first rule) captures RRU.PrbTotDl PRB pressure - the data slice consumes - and surfaces DRB.UEThpDl evidence of the guarantee breach; slice apply-static then enlarges the slice's STATIC PRB reservation and monitors the applied policy (its built-in validation covers the control-confirmation role); a final kpm observe-ue closes the loop by verifying DRB.UEThpDl recovery against the 50 Mbit/s guarantee. No operator template is reused unchanged: the intent is a specific change plan, not a named procedure, and a novel 3-step chain fits the 1–4 step preference. Step 1: kpm/observe-ue reads per-UE/DRB KPM records (DRB.UEThpDl, DRB.RlcSduDelayDl) to establish what is wrong with the VIP's connection; observe-ue is preferred over observe-rru because the complaint is one UE, not cell load. Step 2: rc/rc-control is the only per-UE bearer flow-mapping actuator (E2SM-RC style 1, action 2 QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping) and includes E2 CONTROL-ACK validation, satisfying 'fix that one UE only' and the RC-last rule. TC and slice are excluded: TC is transport/queue treatment and slice is PRB partitioning — neither fixes QoS-flow mapping and both would change state beyond the single UE; the observe-diagnose-optimize template was rejected for the same reason (it adds slice/TC writes). Risks: (1) the RC step must be gated on KPM evidence of a per-UE DRB anomaly with otherwise normal cell PRB utilisation — if KPM shows cell-wide congestion instead, abort this chain and reroute to a TC/slice workflow; (2) on the FlexRIC emulator the RC control is acknowledged but has no effect on later KPIs, so treat the CONTROL-ACK as delivery confirmation, not proof of improvement. Next best action: run kpm/observe-ue, compare the VIP UE's DRB throughput/delay against cell aggregates, then execute rc/rc-control only if the bearer mapping is implicated.

planner_plan.rationale: KPM leads per triage rule: observe-rru captures cell PRB load (RRU.PrbTotDl/Ul) to rule out cell-wide congestion in the boardroom cell, and observe-ue captures the VIP UE's DRB.UEThpDl and DRB.RlcSduDelayDl as per-UE bearer evidence; both are read-only. RC closes the loop last: rc-control sends the E2SM-RC style 1 / action 2 QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping (DRB 5, QFI 10, DL) for the single target UE and confirms E2 CONTROL-ACK, matching 'fix the flow mapping for that one UE only'. Gate rc-control on KPM evidence: proceed only if cell PRB load is normal while the UE's throughput/delay is anomalous (bearer-mapping fault); if the cell is saturated, stop before control, since congestion mitigation is outside this intent. TC excluded (transport-wide queue/AQM policy would affect other traffic, not a per-UE flow mapping) and SLICE excluded (slice PRB writer not required, consistent with the operator's prior rejection of unnecessary writers); no template reused because observe-diagnose-optimize carries unneeded SLICE/TC writers. Risks: rc-control is bound to UE amf_ue_ngap_id 1, so verify it resolves to the VIP UE before sending; on the FlexRIC emulator the control is ACKed but has no effect on later KPIs, so validate success via E2 CONTROL-ACK rather than a post-change KPM delta. Next best action: run both KPM observations, compare the UE's KPIs against cell load, then trigger rc-control only if bearer mis-mapping is implicated.

planner_plan.rationale: SLO is latency/jitter for the gaming tenant under full-venue contention, so: kpm first (observe-ue) to baseline RLC SDU delay, UE throughput and PRB load from the shared KPM bus - the congestion evidence both control agents consume. slice apply-static reserves gaming-tenant PRBs (STATIC profile) so competing tenants cannot starve it on shared cells (consumes RRU.PrbTotDl from kpm). tc apply-codel bounds standing queue delay/bufferbloat on the bearer path - the direct lever for RTT < 20 ms and jitter < 5 ms (consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl from kpm). rc last per policy: maps the gaming QoS flow (QFI 10) onto dedicated DRB 5 and confirms the E2 CONTROL-ACK as control validation. Risks: on this emulator the RC control is acknowledged but has no effect on later KPIs, so treat the ack as confirmation only, not assurance; slice reservation sizing relies on the pre-event kpm window and may undersize at peak. Next best action: execute the chain before gates open, then re-run kpm observe-ue during the match and tighten the slice PRB reservation or escalate tc to the full profile (apply-all) if delay KPIs breach the SLO.

planner_plan.rationale: Enforcement intent (hold RTT < 20 ms, jitter < 5 ms under full-venue contention), so control writers are required; this mirrors the operator-accepted KPM→SLICE→TC→RC chain from the similar XR latency-guarantee intent. (1) kpm observe-rru first: baseline cell PRB load as the venue fills and supplies the data downstream agents consume (RRU.PrbTotDl for slice, DRB.RlcSduDelayDl for tc). (2) slice apply-static: STATIC PRB reservation isolates the gaming tenant from competing tenants on the same cells — monitor alone would not protect capacity. (3) tc apply-codel: CoDel AQM bounds queueing delay and jitter (bufferbloat) on the bearer path, the direct lever for the 5 ms jitter target. (4) rc rc-control last: maps the gaming tenant's QoS flow to DRB 5 and confirms E2 CONTROL-ACK as final actuation/validation, per the RC-last rule. Risks: on this emulator RC control is acknowledged but has no effect on later KPIs, so treat RC as confirmation only and verify via KPM/RLC telemetry; size the STATIC reservation to avoid starving other tenants; CoDel covers transport queueing while the slice reservation covers radio-side contention. Next best action: once the venue is full, re-run kpm observe-ue to check DRB.RlcSduDelayDl against the 20 ms/5 ms budget and re-trigger this chain if breached.

planner_plan.rationale: Observation: camera-inspection uploads (bulk traffic) contend with AGV control messages for cell PRBs and inflate RLC SDU queueing delay, breaching the 10 ms cycle deadline. kpm runs first (read-only) to capture the contention evidence - PRB utilisation, camera-upload throughput (DRB.UEThpDl) and DRB.RlcSduDelayDl vs the 10 ms deadline - and its outputs satisfy downstream dependencies (RRU.PrbTotDl for slice, DRB.RlcSduDelayDl for tc). slice/apply-static is the radio-resource fix: a STATIC PRB reservation isolates the AGV control slice from the camera-inspection slice so uploads cannot starve AGV scheduling. tc/apply-codel is the queueing fix: CoDel AQM bounds standing queue delay and bufferbloat on the bearer path so AGV packets are not stuck behind upload bursts. rc/rc-control is last per policy: it maps the AGV QoS flow (QFI 10) to a dedicated DRB 5 and confirms the E2 CONTROL-ACK, validating the per-UE bearer decision. Risks: on this emulator the RC control is acknowledged but has no effect on later KPIs, so treat the ack as confirmation only; a STATIC reservation can strand capacity if camera load drops; TC acts on the transport path and cannot recover radio-level contention on its own. Next best action: re-run kpm (observe-ue) during an active upload window after the slice and TC changes and verify DRB.RlcSduDelayDl stays under 10 ms; if not, tighten the slice PRB reservation or escalate to the TC full profile (apply-all).

Radio-resource fix: slice/apply-static reserves PRBs (STATIC profile) to isolate the AGV control slice from inspection uploads, consuming RRU.PrbTotDl from the KPM step. Queueing fix: tc/apply-codel bounds queueing delay and bufferbloat on the bearer path, consuming DRB.RlcSduDelayDl from KPM. RC last: rc-control maps the AGV QoS flow onto a dedicated DRB and confirms E2 CONTROL-ACK, adding bearer-level isolation and validating the control decision. This mirrors the operator-accepted KPM->SLICE->TC->RC chain; a TC-only chain was previously rejected for missing SLICE, and this intent explicitly demands fixes at both levels, so the single-step transport-qos template is insufficient. Risks: on the FlexRIC emulator RC control is ACKed but does not move later KPIs, and a static PRB partition reduces peak capacity for the inspection uploads - schedule a follow-up KPM check to confirm AGV deadline recovery and acceptable upload throughput.

Risks: two-hour session needs periodic re-measurement to catch tenant load shifts, and TC alone cannot fix radio congestion if slice headroom is exhausted. Next best action: run KPM to baseline current cell/transport utilization, then apply the slice policy before session start and re-validate with RC within the first minutes.

rationale.next_best_action: Execute the chain, then re-run kpm observe-ue after ~5 minutes to verify DRB.UEThpDl >= 15 Mbit/s and DRB.RlcSduDelayDl < 50 ms; if throughput sags, re-apply slice apply-static with a larger reservation, and if delay rises, re-run tc apply-all. Schedule periodic re-execution for the remainder of the 2-hour session.
rationale.observations: No operator template fits unchanged: 'observe-diagnose-optimize' uses slice in monitor (read-only) mode, which would not reserve PRBs for the clinic UE, so a novel chain was composed. kpm observe-ue targets the exact SLO metrics (UE throughput, RLC SDU delay) while agent-level produces still supply RRU.PrbTotDl for the slice step. tc apply-all (vs apply-codel) adds traffic classification/partitioning plus the RLC monitor, better suited to a 2-hour multi-tenant window.
rationale.risks: On the FlexRIC emulator, RC control is acknowledged but has no effect on later KPIs, so rc-control validates the control path only, not the throughput guarantee. The STATIC slice profile is a fixed reservation; over-reserving could starve other tenants, so size it to roughly the 15-20 Mbit/s the session needs. tc only fixes transport queueing; radio-side congestion must be absorbed by the slice reservation. These are one-shot suite actions, not a 2-hour closed loop.
rationale.summary: The ultrasound SLO has two fronts: radio capacity (>=15 Mbit/s while co-tenants load the cell) and transport delay (<50 ms one-way while co-tenants load the link). KPM first gathers evidence (DRB.UEThpDl, DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, RRU.PrbTotDl); slice applies a STATIC PRB reservation to isolate the clinic UE's capacity in the shared cell; tc runs the full AQM/classification profile to control queueing delay on the shared transport; rc is last, mapping the ultrasound QoS flow to a DRB and confirming the E2 CONTROL-ACK.

Risks: evening peak recurrence if policy is time-window dependent, and bulk-traffic throughput reduction as an expected trade-off. Next best action: execute the chain, verify video-call latency recovery via RC, then schedule recurring KPM checks for the evening window.

planner_plan.rationale: Observation: evening bulk downloads saturate sector 12 PRB, and the resulting queue buildup (bufferbloat) adds latency that lags interactive video calls. Plan: (1) kpm/observe-rru first to capture PRB utilisation and RLC SDU delay evidence for diagnosis; (2) slice/apply-static to partition PRB capacity per slice so conversational video traffic is isolated from bulk best-effort during peak hours; (3) tc/apply-codel to mitigate queueing delay/bufferbloat on the bearer path; (4) rc/rc-control last to push the per-UE QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping for video UEs and confirm the E2 CONTROL-ACK. Dependency check: slice consumes RRU.PrbTotDl and tc consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, both produced by the KPM step; rc has no unmet requires. This mirrors the operator-accepted pattern for capacity-headroom intents (KPM,SLICE,TC,RC) — TC must not be dropped, as a prior proposal without it was rejected. Risks: on the FlexRIC emulator RC control is acknowledged but has no effect on later KPIs, so treat the ACK as confirmation only; the STATIC slice reservation will cap bulk-download throughput by design. Next best action: execute the chain, then run a follow-up kpm/observe-rru window in the evening peak to verify video-call delay improvement before making the policy persistent.

planner_plan.rationale: Evening video lag with bulk downloads saturating sector 12 indicates sector congestion plus bufferbloat, so the chain observes, partitions, de-queues, then actuates. KPM observe-rru first supplies congestion evidence and produces RRU.PrbTotDl and DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, which downstream slice (consumes RRU.PrbTotDl) and tc (consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl) require. Slice apply-static reserves PRB capacity to isolate video traffic from bulk downloads; tc apply-codel mitigates queueing delay on the bearer path; rc rc-control is last, mapping the video QoS flow to a DRB and confirming the E2 CONTROL-ACK. This matches the operator-accepted KPM->SLICE->TC->RC pattern for capacity-headroom intents (TC must not be dropped). Risks: on the FlexRIC emulator RC control is acknowledged but does not move later KPIs, so treat RC as actuation/confirmation only; a post-change KPM re-check is recommended as a follow-up run rather than a fifth step to stay within the 1-4 step preference.

planner_plan.rationale: Root-cause triage for the 20 ms V2X budget starts with observation: KPM observe-ue reads UE/DRB-level KPM records (DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, UE throughput, PRB load) to localize whether delay accumulates in radio resources or transport. Slice apply-static then corrects the slice allocation with a STATIC PRB reservation for the platoon slice and monitors the result; it consumes RRU.PrbTotDl, provided by the earlier KPM step. TC apply-codel corrects transport queueing (CoDel AQM against bufferbloat/queueing delay); it consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, also provided by KPM. RC rc-control runs last as the actuation/validation step, pushing the QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping for the V2X bearer and confirming the E2 CONTROL-ACK. All selected cards are status 'ready'; dependencies (slice<-RRU.PrbTotDl, tc<-DRB.RlcSduDelayDl) are satisfied by the KPM step; chain length is 4. Risks: on the FlexRIC emulator the RC control is acknowledged but has no effect on later KPIs, so latency improvement must be attributed to the slice/TC changes; STATIC PRB reservation and CoDel act on different segments, so residual delay may require a second loop. Next best action: execute the chain, then re-run KPM observe-ue to verify 99.99% of V2X messages arrive within 20 ms before declaring the trial healthy.

SLICE apply-static corrects PRB reservation for the platooning slice (consumes RRU.PrbTotDl provided by KPM) and includes post-apply monitoring of UE-to-slice association. TC apply-codel corrects transport queueing delay/bufferbloat on the bearer path (consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl provided by KPM). RC rc-control is last per the RC-final rule: it pushes the per-UE QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping (DRB 5, QFI 10) and confirms the E2 CONTROL-ACK, validating the applied control decision. RC is deliberately excluded: its only control is a per-UE DL QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping (DRB 5/QFI 10/DL), irrelevant to uplink queues, and its card warns the CONTROL-ACK has no KPI effect on this emulator. All selected cards are status ready (none deprecated); all consumes are satisfied by earlier steps; 4 steps within the 1-4 preference. Risks: STATIC slice reservation is coarse and may need retuning to camera bitrates; CoDel treats queue delay, not capacity, so sustained relief depends on slice isolation holding at peak. Next best action: execute the chain ahead of the 18:00 peak and re-run kpm observe-ue during peak; if uplink KPIs remain degraded, escalate tc to apply-all (adds RLC monitor) or re-profile the slice reservation.

planner_plan.rationale: Observation: evening residential peak (19:00-23:00) shows median DRB.UEThpDl <5 Mbit/s with slow page loads; stated root causes are inter-slice PRB contention and bloated shared bearer queues. Plan: kpm observe-rru first for a read-only baseline (RRU.PrbTotDl, DRB.UEThpDl, DRB.RlcSduDelayDl), which also satisfies slice's consume (RRU.PrbTotDl) and tc's consume (DRB.RlcSduDelayDl); slice apply-static then partitions PRBs per slice (STATIC profile) to stop the slice contention and lift median throughput; tc apply-codel adds CoDel AQM on the bearer path to drain the bloated shared queues and cut downlink queueing delay for snappy page loads; final kpm observe-ue validates the target (median DRB.UEThpDl >20 Mbit/s, reduced DRB.RlcSduDelayDl). RC is deliberately excluded: its per-UE QoS-flow-to-DRB control is out of scope for slice PRB reservation and queue management per its card, and on this emulator its control is acknowledged but has no KPI effect. Risks: a static PRB split can starve a bursty slice if the evening traffic mix shifts, and CoDel fixes queue delay but not radio capacity, so throughput gains hinge on the slice reconfiguration landing first. Next best action: execute the chain; if the step-4 check still shows median DL throughput <20 Mbit/s, re-run slice apply-static with a revised PRB reservation before considering any per-UE bearer changes.

KPM runs first to baseline PRB utilisation and load, supplying RRU.PrbTotDl (consumed by slice) and DRB.RlcSduDelayDl (consumed by tc). Slice apply-static then partitions PRBs per slice so research transfers cannot crowd out the lecture slice while its reserved capacity prevents starvation of the research slice. TC apply-all finishes with CoDel/ECN AQM, classification and shaping on the bearer path to stop the dataset transfers inflating everyone's queues, with per-class treatment protecting the lecture stream; its RLC monitor yields queue_stats to validate queueing delay after the change. RC is deliberately excluded: its card scopes it to per-UE radio bearer control and explicitly not for slice PRB reservation or queue management, its fixed control targets a single UE (impractical for 400), and on this emulator the control is acknowledged but has no KPI effect. No template fits unchanged (slice-assurance is read-only slice monitor; observe-diagnose-optimize forces an out-of-scope RC step), so this is a novel 3-step chain. Risks: a static PRB split may misallocate if lecture/research load shifts, and TC shaping must be sized so the research slice keeps throughput. Next best action: execute the chain, then re-run kpm observe-ue to confirm DRB.UEThpDl for lecture UEs stays stable and the research slice retains throughput; adjust the static split or shaping rate if either drifts.

planner_plan.rationale: Observation: 400 concurrent lecture streams compete with research-slice bulk transfers, so both radio capacity pressure (PRB) and transport queue inflation (bufferbloat) are in play. Plan: KPM first (observe-rru) to capture PRB utilisation and RLC SDU delay evidence; slice apply-static to reserve PRB per slice so the lecture slice is isolated from research transfers while the research slice keeps reserved capacity (no starvation); tc apply-codel so large dataset transfers cannot inflate everyone's queues (stutter-free streaming); rc last to map the lecture QoS flow to a dedicated DRB and confirm via E2 CONTROL-ACK. Dependencies hold: slice consumes RRU.PrbTotDl and tc consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, both produced by the earlier kpm step. This matches the operator-accepted chain [KPM, SLICE, TC, RC] for capacity/QoS intents; the rejected [KPM, SLICE, RC] variant was missing TC, which is essential here for queue management. Risk: on the FlexRIC emulator RC control is acknowledged but does not affect later KPIs, so treat rc-control as validation only. Next best action: after the chain, re-run kpm observe-ue to verify lecture-stream throughput and delay improved and research-slice throughput was not starved.

Step 1 kpm/observe-rru captures the PRB-utilisation baseline and produces RRU.PrbTotDl, satisfying slice's consumes. RC is excluded (its card forbids slice-PRB use and its control is ack-only with no KPI effect on this emulator) and TC is out of scope for PRB partitioning; the slice-assurance template was rejected because its slice-first order violates the consumes rule and its rc-control step is unnecessary here. Risks: slice monitor proves configuration, not airtime fairness under load. Next best action if the observed PRB share or UE throughput falls short of the reservation: run slice apply-static to enforce the 20% profile, then rerun kpm observe-ue to validate impact.

A second KPM step, observe-ue, reads DRB.UEThpDl to confirm tenant users experience the reserved capacity.
rationale.next_best_action: Run the chain. If the reservation is not in force, follow with slice apply-static and re-run KPM validation. If it is in force but UE throughput lags, correlate RRU.PrbTotDl congestion and escalate or extend the chain with a TC step.
rationale.observations: Intent is pure assurance: verify the 20% PRB reservation is active and that tenant UEs actually receive that capacity. No control decision is applied or validated, so RC is excluded (its bearer-mapping control is unrelated to slice PRB and is ack-only with no KPI effect on the emulator). TC is out of scope: no transport/queue symptoms. The slice-assurance template was not reused because its rc-control step is unnecessary here and its SLICE-before-KPM order violates slice's consumes rule.
rationale.risks: kpm appears twice for before/after evidence; if the router rejects duplicate agents, fall back to [kpm, slice]. If slice monitor shows the reservation missing or mismatched, do not silently re-apply policy. Low UE throughput with the reservation in force may indicate cell congestion rather than a slice fault.

Next best action: execute the chain, diff baseline vs post-change per-slice PRB utilisation, and attach the delta report to CHG-2231 for sign-off.

RC is excluded: no control decision is applied or validated, and on this emulator rc-control is acknowledged but has no effect on later KPIs. TC is out of scope (transport queues, not slice policy). slice/apply-static is deliberately avoided because it would mutate the very policy being inspected. Risks: the ~1 s observation window may miss transient SLA violations, and KPM metrics are cell-wide unless correlated with the slice's UE associations from the monitor report. Next best action: if measured load is inconsistent with the reserved PRB policy, re-run as slice/apply-static (or tc for delay/bufferbloat causes) followed by kpm as a post-control verification; optionally add kpm/observe-ue first if DRB.UEThpDl or RLC SDU delay evidence is needed for the latency side of the SLA.

Step 1 (kpm/observe-rru) satisfies the 'KPM first for observation/diagnosis' rule, establishes cell-level PRB utilisation, and supplies RRU.PrbTotDl which the slice agent consumes. Step 2 (slice/monitor) is the read-only slice action: it returns the configured per-slice PRB reservation (Tenant C's contracted share) and UE-to-slice associations identifying Tenant C's UEs. Step 3 (kpm/observe-ue) then reads per-UE/DRB throughput (DRB.UEThpDl) so actual usage of Tenant C's associated UEs can be compared against the reserved share. Chain is 3 steps (within the 1-4 preference), all agents are status 'ready' (no deprecated cards), and every consumes/requires dependency is met by an earlier step. planner_plan.rationale: Intent is a read-only review of slice PRB quotas vs measured usage on cell 3, so no control actuation is warranted. KPM runs first (observe-rru) to collect current PRB utilisation evidence (RRU.PrbTotDl/PrbTotUl) per the observe-first rule. RC is omitted: the task applies no control decision, and the RC card explicitly excludes slice PRB work (its rc-control would push an unrelated bearer mapping). TC is excluded as transport-only. Risks: KPM gives cell-level PRB totals, so per-slice usage must be inferred by correlating slice.ue_association with utilisation; emulator KPIs may be synthetic. Next best action: if the review shows quota/usage mismatch, re-run with slice apply-static under change control, then add KPM post-check (and RC only if a bearer-level validation is required).

planner_plan.rationale: Intent is a per-class transport rate cap (10 Mbit/s on the software-update class), so TC is the required writer: it is the only card with traffic_shaping/transport_qos capability and a write scope on tc_control. The apply-all full profile is chosen over apply-codel because shaping/classification (not CoDel AQM alone) is what enforces a hard class cap. KPM (observe-ue) runs first to satisfy TC's consumed DRB.RlcSduDelayDl and to baseline per-UE throughput/delay (DRB.UEThpDl) for before/after validation of the cap. RC is excluded: its only control action is QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping (not rate shaping), it is acknowledged-but-ineffective on the FlexRIC emulator, and past intents show unneeded writers get rejected ('forbidden writer'). Slice is excluded: PRB reservation is radio-side partitioning, not transport class treatment. No operator template is named by the intent, so a minimal 2-step chain is composed; risk is that TC's fixed suite profiles may not expose an exact 10 Mbit/s parameter, so verify the applied tc.policy output against the interactive-flow delay KPIs after execution.

planner_plan.rationale: Observation: the intent is a prescriptive per-class transport policy (cap the software-update download class at 10 Mbit/s on the shared bearer path), not a diagnosis or triage task, so no upfront KPM observation is required. TC is the only executable card with traffic_shaping and traffic-classification capability on the bearer path; 'apply-all' runs the full profile (classification + shaping + AQM) needed to enforce an explicit 10 Mbit/s rate cap, whereas 'apply-codel' is AQM-only and cannot set a rate limit. The built-in RLC monitor in apply-all supplies the DRB.RlcSduDelayDl input TC consumes and yields queue evidence that interactive flows are protected. This matches the operator-accepted TC-only chain for the closely related transport bufferbloat intent. Exclusions: KPM omitted (read-only evidence not requested; can be appended post-control if verification is wanted); SLICE omitted (PRB partitioning is radio-side, not transport shaping); RC omitted (its fixed QoS-flow-to-DRB control is not a rate cap and its card forbids use for queue management). Risks: on the FlexRIC emulator the control may be acknowledged with simulated effect; the shaper class must match the software-update traffic classifier to avoid mis-shaping interactive flows. Next best action: execute tc/apply-all, then optionally re-run with kpm/observe-ue to confirm the download-class throughput is capped at 10 Mbit/s.

planner_plan.rationale: Observation: the intent is per-class transport treatment on the bearer path (voice in its own queue, served ahead of best-effort), which maps directly to the TC service model's traffic classification, partitioning and AQM capabilities. Plan: single-step TC chain, matching the operator-accepted pattern for transport QoS intents (bufferbloat -> [TC]) and avoiding unnecessary writers. Action apply-all (full profile + RLC monitor) is chosen over apply-codel because CoDel AQM alone manages one queue's delay and does not create per-class queues; the full profile performs the classification/partitioning needed to give voice a dedicated higher-priority queue, and its built-in RLC monitor satisfies TC's DRB.RlcSduDelayDl consumption while producing RLC.queue_stats for verification. KPM omitted: this is a direct control intent, not observation/diagnosis, and TC self-monitors via E2SM-RLC. RC omitted: E2SM-RC QFI-to-DRB mapping is radio bearer control, explicitly out of scope for queue management, and its control is ack-only with no KPI effect on the emulator. SLICE omitted: PRB partitioning is radio-side, not bearer-path queueing, and past rejections penalize unneeded write scopes. Risks: on the FlexRIC emulator the policy effect may be simulated; voice prioritization depends on correct DSCP/flow classification, so misclassified voice would not get the dedicated queue. Next best action: run tc/apply-all, then inspect RLC.queue_stats (optionally a follow-up kpm observe-ue) to confirm the voice queue shows lower delay/jitter than best-effort before closing the loop.

planner_plan.rationale: CR 4411's full queue-management profile (classification, partitioning, shaping, CoDel) maps exactly to TC's full-profile suite, so tc:apply-all is the actuation step; the transport-qos template (apply-codel only) under-covers the requested profile and is not reused. kpm:observe-ue runs first because TC consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, which only KPM produces, and it captures a pre-change bearer-delay baseline from UE/DRB-oriented KPM records. Slice is excluded: the partitioning in scope is TC bearer-path partitioning, not slice PRB reservation (both cards forbid crossing that boundary, and an unrequested SLICE write was previously rejected). RC is excluded: the control decision is applied and acknowledged within TC's tc_control write scope; RC's QoS-flow-to-DRB control is radio bearer mapping, explicitly not for queue management, and its ack has no KPI effect on this emulator. Risks: tc_control is a single writer — if TC is busy with another loop, serialize rather than parallel-run; shaping/CoDel ramp-up may transiently raise RLC SDU delay; emulator TC changes may not show in KPM deltas, so judge success via TC's RLC.queue_stats output. Next best action: execute kpm then tc, then run a follow-up KPM observe-ue check to confirm DRB.RlcSduDelayDl improvement before closing CR 4411.

Step 1 (kpm/observe-ue) captures the DRB.RlcSduDelayDl baseline, which is also the data tc consumes, satisfying the dependency rule. Step 3 (kpm/observe-ue) re-measures RLC SDU delay to confirm the queue drained, closing the loop. RC is excluded: its card explicitly forbids queue management (TC scope) and its emulator control is acknowledged but has no effect on KPIs, so the 'RC last' heuristic does not apply to this transport-layer decision. Slice is excluded: no PRB partitioning or slice reconfiguration is required. No operator template matches (transport-qos omits the required measurement phase; observe-diagnose-optimize adds irrelevant slice monitoring and an RC bearer control that its card explicitly forbids for queue management). The 1 s KPM timescale may need a longer sampling window to resolve intermittent 40 ms spikes and the post-control delta.

RC is excluded: its card forbids queue management (it only does QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping, and its control has no KPI effect on this emulator), so TC is the correct final actuator. Slice is excluded: no PRB partitioning requested. Risks: apply-codel is the closest available action to explicit ECN marking — if the deployment's ECN profile differs, re-run TC with apply-all; emulator KPIs may respond slowly, so allow a measurement window before judging step 3. planner_plan.rationale: Read-only evidence chain for the service-credit dispute: observe-rru captures cell-level PRB load (RRU.PrbTotDl/Ul) for the two campus cells, and observe-ue captures the requested per-UE throughput (DRB.UEThpDl) and delay (DRB.RlcSduDelayDl) from the shared KPM bus. No control agents are selected: the intent explicitly says make no changes, so rc-control, apply-codel and apply-static are excluded; the 'is control warranted' review is an offline judgment on the KPM snapshot, and rc-report would only add RRC state, not throughput/delay evidence. No operator template is reused because every template containing control steps (slice-assurance, observe-diagnose-optimize, transport-qos) would violate the no-change constraint, so a novel 1-agent chain is composed. Risks: the KPM snapshot reflects current conditions only and cannot retroactively evidence last week's service, so historical records outside RIC scope may be needed for the dispute; per-UE granularity depends on the KPM subscription covering the correct two cell IDs. Next best action: run the chain scoped to the two campus cells, attach the kpm.snapshot to the dispute case, and if sustained congestion or delay is observed, propose a follow-up control chain (e.g., slice monitor + TC) requiring explicit customer/operator approval before execution.

Next best action: execute the chain; if both sources agree at ~90% with matching UE associations, treat the alarm as genuine and escalate to capacity/slice triage; if KPM reads 90% while slice state and throughput are flat, flag a KPM counter/subscription glitch and re-subscribe the KPM service model.

KPM produces DRB.RlcSduDelayDl (per-UE/DRB RLC SDU delay) from the shared KPM bus, and the observe-ue action reads UE/DRB-oriented KPM records, matching the per-bearer cell-4 readout. No template matches a pure delay readout (transport-qos applies CoDel control; the other templates add SLICE/TC/RC control steps that are unnecessary and would risk forbidden-writer rejection per operator history). Single step satisfies all constraints: KPM has no requires/consumes, is status ready, and is the mandated first agent for observation. Next best action: run observe-ue, surface DRB.RlcSduDelayDl per bearer to the latency dashboard; if sustained delay anomalies appear, escalate to a KPM->TC (or KPM->SLICE) diagnose-and-mitigate chain.

planner_plan.rationale: Observation: reported imbalance (eMBB ~15% of reservation idle, URLLC saturated) needs measured PRB evidence before control, so KPM leads with observe-rru (RRU.PrbTotDl per slice). Dependency check: slice consumes RRU.PrbTotDl, which step 1 produces; slice apply-static then re-applies the STATIC profile with a revised eMBB->URLLC PRB split sized from the measured load, and its built-in monitor reports new reservations/UE associations. A second kpm observe-rru gives an independent before/after PRB-utilization verification. Exclusions: rc is per-UE radio-bearer control and its card explicitly forbids slice PRB reservation (and on this emulator its control does not move KPIs); tc targets transport queues, not PRB partitioning. Risks: apply-static rewrites the full reservation set, so the new split must be encoded explicitly (shift PRBs roughly proportional to idle vs saturated share); a single static re-partition may under- or over-shoot. Next best action: execute the chain, diff per-slice RRU.PrbTotDl pre/post, and if URLLC utilization remains >~90%, re-run with a larger shifted reservation; swap the final step to kpm observe-ue if per-UE throughput (DRB.UEThpDl) confirmation is preferred.

planner_plan.rationale: The intent requires sizing a guaranteed PRB share from measured peak demand, then enforcing it. KPM runs first (observation rule) via observe-rru to capture RRU.PrbTotDl, which is exactly the data the slice agent consumes for capacity partitioning. The slice agent then applies the STATIC profile (apply-static), which both sets the PRB reservation and validates it by reporting UE-to-slice associations and reserved capacity. RC is deliberately excluded: its card explicitly forbids use for slice PRB reservation, and its control scope is per-UE bearer mapping, not slice partitioning, so the slice agent's built-in apply-and-monitor suite is the correct final control step. No operator template matches this sizing-then-enforce procedure (slice-assurance ends with an inappropriate rc-control), so a novel 2-step chain is composed. All requires/consumes are satisfied: kpm consumes nothing; slice consumes RRU.PrbTotDl produced by the preceding kpm step. Risk: the STATIC profile is fixed once applied; if the robotics line's peak demand shifts, re-run the chain to resize. Next best action: execute kpm.observe-rru over a window covering the line's peak production cycle, then feed the measured peak PRB demand into slice.apply-static.

planner_plan.rationale: Observation: Operator A under-use vs operator B congestion on a shared carrier is a per-slice PRB capacity-partitioning problem, so measurement must precede re-partitioning. Step 1 (kpm/observe-rru) runs a read-only KPM window capturing both operators' PRB utilisation (RRU.PrbTotDl/Ul), satisfying slice's consumes requirement (RRU.PrbTotDl) and the KPM-first rule. Step 2 (slice/apply-static) re-partitions reserved PRB capacity between the operator slices via the STATIC profile within the sharing agreement and self-validates by monitoring slice indications and reporting UE-to-slice associations and reserved capacity. RC is excluded: its only control is per-UE QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping, its card explicitly forbids slice PRB reservation, and emulator CONTROL-ACKs have no effect on later KPIs; TC is excluded as it governs transport queues, not radio capacity. Risks: on the FlexRIC emulator the slice control may be acknowledged without shifting subsequent KPIs, and one short KPM window may under-sample bursty congestion on B. Next best action: schedule a follow-up kpm/observe-rru check after apply-static to confirm the new partition and B's congestion relief; widen the measurement window or add kpm/observe-ue (UE throughput evidence) if utilisation remains skewed.

Step 1 (kpm/observe-rru) measures both operators' PRB utilisation on the shared carrier and produces RRU.PrbTotDl, which the slice agent consumes, satisfying the data-dependency rule. RC is excluded because its card explicitly forbids slice PRB reservation and its control is per-UE bearer mapping with no KPI effect on this emulator; TC is excluded because the congestion is radio-side PRB, not transport queueing. All agents are status ready; no deprecated cards used.

planner_plan.rationale: Observation: the intent requires measuring both operators on the shared carrier, then re-partitioning radio capacity. kpm/observe-rru runs first (read-only) and supplies RRU.PrbTotDl/PrbTotUl evidence of under-utilisation by A and congestion for B. slice/apply-static follows: it consumes RRU.PrbTotDl (dependency satisfied by step 1), exercises the capacity_partitioning capability to re-partition PRB reservation within the sharing agreement, and its built-in monitor reports per-slice reserved capacity and UE-to-slice associations for both operators. rc is placed last per policy to apply/validate the control decision via E2 CONTROL-ACK. TC is excluded: the intent is radio PRB partitioning, not transport queueing/delay, and no step consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl. The chain matches the operator-accepted [KPM, SLICE, RC] pattern for slice-capacity intents, uses only ready (non-deprecated) cards, and stays within the 1-4 step bound. Risks: the STATIC profile is a coarse re-partition, so the applied reservation must encode each operator's contracted share; on the FlexRIC emulator rc-control is acknowledged but does not change later KPIs, so treat the ACK as control-path validation only. Next best action: execute the chain, then re-run kpm/observe-rru to confirm operator A's usage rises toward its contracted share while B's congestion clears.

planner_plan.rationale: Observation: the intent is transport AQM on the default bearer (CoDel drops -> ECN marking) plus confirmation, so TC is the actuator and RC closes the loop. KPM runs first with observe-ue because TC consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, which only KPM produces, and it captures a pre-change UE/DRB baseline. TC uses apply-all, not apply-codel: apply-codel would re-assert the drop-based profile we are switching away from, while the full-profile suite is the TC path to ECN marking and its RLC monitor yields RLC.queue_stats as change evidence. RC runs last with rc-control per the rule that RC finalizes chains that apply/validate a control decision, matching operator-accepted TC->RC patterns for ECN/CoDel verification intents; its E2 CONTROL-ACK is the 'change went through' signal. Slice is excluded (PRB partitioning out of scope); the transport-qos and observe-diagnose-optimize templates are not reused because both pin apply-codel, contradicting the ECN switch. Risks: on this emulator RC control is ACKed but has no effect on later KPIs, so the ACK confirms delivery, not KPI impact; the TC card exposes no explicit ECN action, so tc.policy output must be checked to confirm ECN marking was actually applied; since RC must be last, post-change queue evidence comes from TC's RLC monitor rather than a trailing KPM check. Next best action: execute kpm->tc->rc, then verify tc.policy reports ECN and RLC.queue_stats show marks instead of drops; if tc.policy still reports CoDel, re-run TC once an explicit ECN action is available.

planner_plan.rationale: Rollback to the static baseline is a slice-control action, so slice/apply-static is the actuator: it pushes the STATIC profile over E2SM-SLICE and its built-in monitor reports acceptance (slice.policy, slice.ue_association, reserved capacity). KPM runs first to satisfy slice's RRU.PrbTotDl consumption and capture a pre-rollback baseline (observation-first rule). A final KPM observe-rru provides the independent post-control measurement check confirming the rollback was accepted and PRB utilisation returned to baseline. RC is excluded: its card forbids use for slice PRB reservation and its E2SM-RC control targets per-UE bearer mapping, not slice policy; TC is out of scope (transport/queues). Risks: on this emulator control acks may not move later KPIs, so confirmation rests on the slice monitor output plus the pre/post KPM delta, and short observation windows may miss slow convergence. Next best action: execute the chain, diff pre/post RRU.PrbTotDl and slice.ue_association against the static baseline, and re-run slice/apply-static if the post-check diverges.

planner_plan.rationale: Rollback to the static baseline is a slice-control action, so the slice agent's 'apply-static' (STATIC profile + built-in monitor) is the core step; its monitor mode reports slice indications, UE-to-slice associations and reserved capacity, which is the authoritative confirmation that the rollback was accepted. The slice card consumes RRU.PrbTotDl, which only KPM produces, so KPM must run first — this also captures a pre-rollback KPI baseline. A final KPM 'observe-rru' provides the post-control measurement check to verify PRB utilisation settled at the static partitioning. RC is deliberately excluded: its card forbids use for slice PRB reservation (it is per-UE bearer control, and on this emulator its CONTROL-ACK has no effect on KPIs), so it would add a misleading 'confirmation'. TC is out of scope (transport/queue policies). No deprecated cards were offered. Risk: if the post-rollback KPM window shows PRB distribution inconsistent with the STATIC profile, the E2 node may have accepted but not enforced the policy — next best action is to re-run slice 'apply-static' once, then escalate with the kpm.snapshot evidence attached.

planner_plan.rationale: Diagnosis-first chain for a single VIP UE. Step 1 (kpm/observe-ue) gathers UE/DRB-level evidence (DRB.UEThpDl, DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, PRB utilisation) to determine whether the slowness is bearer-related before any control is applied, satisfying the KPM-first rule for diagnosis. Step 2 (rc/rc-control) is the only agent capable of per-UE QoS-flow-to-DRB remapping (E2SM-RC style 1, action 2) and confirms via E2 CONTROL-ACK, satisfying the RC-last rule; execute it only if KPM evidence implicates the bearer/flow mapping for that UE. TC and SLICE are excluded: the intent is per-UE bearer mapping, not transport queue management or slice PRB partitioning, and no operator template was requested by name, so a novel minimal 2-step chain is composed. Risks: rc-control on this emulator is hard-coded to one UE (amf_ue_ngap_id 1, DRB 5, QFI 10) and is acknowledged but does not move later KPIs, so post-control validation must rely on the RC ack, not KPM deltas; gate the RC step on the KPM snapshot to avoid acting without evidence. Next best action: run kpm/observe-ue, review the UE KPI snapshot, then trigger rc-control for the affected UE if the bearer mapping is confirmed at fault.
