planner_plan.rationale: Observation: the <10 ms delay has two distinct causes, so the chain pairs one control per cause with KPM bookends. Step 1 (kpm/observe-rru) takes a short baseline window on the shared KPM bus, yielding RRU.PrbTotDl (tenant PRB contention) and DRB.RlcSduDelayDl (bearer queueing); KPM leads because the task starts with observation/root-cause triage and it is read-only. Step 2 (slice/apply-static) applies a STATIC PRB reservation to isolate the AR-glasses demo slice from contending tenants; it consumes RRU.PrbTotDl from step 1 and self-monitors after the control. Step 3 (tc/apply-codel) targets the residual queue build-up/bufferbloat with CoDel AQM, consuming DRB.RlcSduDelayDl from step 1. Step 4 (kpm/observe-ue) re-reads UE/DRB KPIs to verify DRB.RlcSduDelayDl is back under the 10 ms budget, closing the loop. RC is deliberately excluded: its card restricts it to per-UE QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping, explicitly not slice PRB reservation or queue management, and on this emulator its control is ACKed without affecting later KPIs, so it would add latency without addressing either cause. Risks: the STATIC profile is coarse if the tenant mix shifts and may need retuning; CoDel treats only the transport path, so radio-side scheduling delay depends on the slice policy holding. Next best action: execute the chain and compare step-4 DRB.RlcSduDelayDl against the step-1 baseline; if the SLO is still breached, re-plan with tc/apply-all (shaping + RLC monitor) or a revised slice PRB profile.

planner_plan.rationale: Intent needs both capacity-share protection and queueing-delay protection, starting from current cell state, so the operator-accepted KPM->SLICE->TC->RC chain is reused with one deliberate adaptation: slice runs apply-static (STATIC PRB reservation) instead of the template's read-only monitor, because 'protect their share of cell capacity' requires active partitioning, not observation. kpm/observe-rru first satisfies the observe-first rule and establishes the pre-rush baseline (RRU.PrbTotDl/Ul, DRB.RlcSduDelayDl); it feeds both downstream consumers (slice consumes RRU.PrbTotDl, tc consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl). tc/apply-codel bounds queueing delay and bufferbloat on the bearer path for the terminal/app traffic class. rc/rc-control is last, validating the per-UE QoS-flow-to-DRB control via E2 CONTROL-ACK. Risks: on the FlexRIC emulator the RC control is acknowledged but has no effect on later KPIs, and the STATIC reservation is fixed-size, so it may need resizing once rush load materializes. Next best action: schedule a follow-up kpm observe-ue check ~10 minutes into the rush to confirm DRB.RlcSduDelayDl stays bounded, and re-run the chain with an adjusted reservation if terminal UEs still show delay.

This mirrors the operator-accepted KPM-SLICE-TC-RC pattern for similar protection intents, uses only ready agents with no conflicts, and all consumes are satisfied by earlier steps. Risks: the STATIC reservation is fixed, so re-check PRB headroom once the rush builds to avoid starving best-effort traffic; on this emulator RC control is acknowledged but does not move later KPIs, so effectiveness must be judged from KPM. Next best action: run the chain now, then re-run kpm observe-rru about 10 minutes into the rush; if DRB.RlcSduDelayDl stays high, escalate tc to apply-all.

planner_plan.rationale: Remote ultrasound needs simultaneous radio and transport assurance: 15 Mbit/s sustained rate and <50 ms one-way delay while other tenants share the cell and backhaul. observe-diagnose-optimize is the only chain covering both domains end-to-end — KPM establishes per-tenant MAC/PHY baseline and detects cell congestion, SLICE enforces dedicated rate/latency policy for the clinic tenant, TC applies transport-side shaping/priority on the shared link, and RC validates the enforced policy and closes the loop. slice-assurance lacks transport coverage (risking backhaul queuing delay), and transport-qos lacks radio/slice enforcement (risking cell-side contention). Risks: two-hour session needs periodic re-measurement to catch tenant load shifts; TC actions alone cannot compensate if slice policy is under-provisioned. Next best action: run the chain, then re-trigger KPM+SLICE reassessment if RC validation shows delay drifting above 50 ms or throughput below 15 Mbit/s.

Risk: policy enforcement may transiently shift bulk throughput; validate against evening-peak KPM deltas before locking changes.

planner_plan.rationale: Observation: the 20 ms / 99.99% V2X target spans radio and transport, so read-only KPM goes first per triage rule, surfacing DRB.RlcSduDelayDl (delay KPI) and RRU.PrbTotDl (load) to localize whether delay accumulates in slice PRB starvation or transport queueing. Slice (consumes RRU.PrbTotDl) then applies the STATIC PRB reservation to secure platoon-slice capacity; TC (consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl) applies CoDel to bound queueing delay/bufferbloat on the bearer path; a closing KPM observe-ue re-measures RLC SDU delay to validate the SLA after control, giving a 4-step closed loop within the limit. RC is deliberately excluded: its QoS-flow-to-DRB control is neither a slice nor a transport fix, its card forbids use for SLICE/TC/KPM, and on this emulator the control is ACKed but does not affect later KPIs. Risks: STATIC reservation takes PRBs from other slices/UEs on the motorway segment; CoDel changes queue treatment and may interact with existing shaping; emulator actuation may not move KPIs, so pre/post deltas can be near zero; short KPM windows under-sample 99.99% tail latency. Next best action: execute the chain and compare pre/post DRB.RlcSduDelayDl distributions against the 20 ms threshold; if tail delay persists with low PRB utilization, re-run TC with apply-all (full profile + RLC monitor) and lengthen the KPM observation window.

Risks: on the FlexRIC emulator RC control is acknowledged but does not change later KPIs, so improvement must be verified by measurement, not by the ACK; if uplink PRB saturation persists after CoDel, escalate to slice apply-static to partition reserved capacity for the cameras. Next best action: execute the chain, then re-run kpm observe-rru post-18:00 to confirm uplink delay and throughput recovery.

planner_plan.rationale: Observation: 18:00 frame drops are a remediation intent with two coupled causes - commuter load crowding the cells (PRB congestion) and growing uplink queues (bufferbloat). KPM runs first per triage rule, supplying RRU.PrbTotDl (consumed by slice) and DRB.RlcSduDelayDl (consumed by tc). Slice apply-static reserves PRB capacity to isolate the CCTV slice from commuter traffic; TC apply-codel applies CoDel AQM to drain the uplink queues; RC rc-control is last to push and confirm the bearer control (E2 CONTROL-ACK), closing the loop. This mirrors the operator-accepted KPM->SLICE->TC->RC pattern for capacity/SLO recovery; writers are justified here because the intent is restoration, not diagnosis. Risks: on this emulator RC CONTROL-ACK does not affect later KPIs, so recovery must be verified by measurement, and a STATIC slice reservation trades capacity away from commuter best-effort traffic. Next best action: execute the chain, then re-run kpm (observe-ue) around 18:00 to confirm uplink throughput and RLC delay recovery for the camera UEs.

planner_plan.rationale: Observation: the 19:00-23:00 degradation has two stated root causes - inter-slice PRB contention and bufferbloat on shared bearer queues - so both SLICE and TC remediation are required; the operator rejected SLICE-less chains for the near-identical downlink-congestion intent and accepted [KPM, SLICE, TC, RC]. KPM leads per the observation-first rule and its card-level produces satisfy downstream consumes: RRU.PrbTotDl for slice, DRB.RlcSduDelayDl for tc (dependency check passes; all cards status ready, none deprecated). slice uses apply-static rather than the template's read-only monitor because monitoring cannot stop PRB fighting - the STATIC profile reserves per-slice PRB capacity. tc uses apply-codel since CoDel AQM directly targets the bloated queues. rc is last per the RC-final rule for chains that apply a control decision, matching the operator-accepted pattern. Risks: rc-control sends a fixed QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping (DRB 5, QFI 10) that the emulator ACKs without KPI effect, so treat it as actuation/ack validation only; a poorly sized STATIC reservation could starve best-effort slices. Next best action: run the chain before the 19:00 window, then re-subscribe kpm (observe-ue) through 23:00 to confirm median DRB.UEThpDl > 20 Mbit/s and falling DRB.RlcSduDelayDl; if throughput recovers but queue delay stays high, escalate tc to apply-all.

planner_plan.rationale: Observation: 400 concurrent lecture streams plus research bulk transfers point to cell saturation (PRB) and transport queue inflation (bufferbloat), so KPM must go first to supply current evidence and the inputs later steps consume (RRU.PrbTotDl for slice, DRB.RlcSduDelayDl for tc); observe-ue captures per-UE throughput (stutter) and RLC SDU delay (queue growth). slice apply-static then partitions PRB per slice so the research slice retains reserved capacity and isolation instead of being crowded out by lecture traffic. tc apply-codel last applies CoDel AQM on the bearer path to keep the bulk-transfer queues short, protecting lecture-stream delay/jitter without dropping research throughput. RC is excluded: per-UE QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping is not needed for this goal and its control has no KPI effect on this emulator. Risks: the STATIC slice profile is a fixed split and may over- or under-serve the research slice as lecture load varies; CoDel fixes queueing, not radio capacity, so persistent PRB saturation can still cause stutters. Next best action: run the chain, then re-run kpm observe-ue to confirm DRB.RlcSduDelayDl falls and DRB.UEThpDl stays stable for both populations, and re-tune the slice partition if research throughput is starved.

planner_plan.rationale: No operator template matches the dual goal (observe-diagnose-optimize is closest but its slice step is read-only), so a novel 4-step chain is composed from ready cards only. (1) kpm/observe-rru first: task requires congestion diagnosis, and KPM supplies RRU.PrbTotDl (consumed by slice) and DRB.RlcSduDelayDl (consumed by tc) as evidence of PRB pressure from 400 streaming UEs plus research bulk transfers. (2) slice/apply-static: per-slice PRB reservation partitions capacity so the lecture slice keeps reserved radio resources (stutter-free) while the research slice retains a guaranteed share (no starvation); slice is scoped to capacity partitioning, not queue policy. (3) tc/apply-codel: CoDel AQM on the bearer path directly stops the large dataset transfers from inflating everyone's queues (bufferbloat/jitter mitigation) and is work-conserving, so research throughput is shaped by queue discipline, not starved. (4) rc/rc-control last: per the rule, RC closes the chain by mapping the lecture QoS flow to a dedicated DRB and validating via E2 CONTROL-ACK. Risks: on the FlexRIC emulator RC control is acknowledged but has no KPI effect, and STATIC slice partitioning is fixed — if DRB.UEThpDl for the research slice drops or RLC SDU delay stays high, the reservation must be retuned. Next best action: execute the chain, then re-run kpm observation to confirm reduced DRB.RlcSduDelayDl and stable per-slice throughput before considering a follow-up slice reconfiguration.

planner_plan.rationale: 400 concurrent lecture streams plus bulk research transfers create two coupled risks: transport bufferbloat (queue inflation, stutter) and slice contention (research starvation). kpm/observe-rru runs first to supply load evidence (RRU.PrbTotDl, DRB.RlcSduDelayDl), satisfying the consumes of slice and tc. slice/apply-static then partitions PRBs per slice with a STATIC reservation so the research slice keeps a guaranteed share (no starvation) while lecture traffic is isolated. tc/apply-codel adds CoDel AQM so the dataset transfers cannot inflate everyone's queues, keeping lecture queueing delay low and the stream stutter-free. rc/rc-control finishes the chain by mapping the lecture QoS flow to a DRB and confirming the E2 CONTROL-ACK as final control validation. This matches the operator-accepted KPM->SLICE->TC->RC pattern for combined capacity/QoS intents (proposals omitting TC were previously rejected). Risk: on the FlexRIC emulator RC control is acknowledged but does not affect later KPIs, so treat RC as confirmation only. Next best action: execute the chain, then re-run kpm observation to verify DRB.RlcSduDelayDl stays low and research-slice throughput (DRB.UEThpDl) is preserved.

Step 1 (kpm/observe-ue) satisfies the KPM-first rule for observation and surfaces DRB.UEThpDl plus RRU.PrbTotDl from the shared KPM bus, quantifying what operator B's UEs actually receive and the carrier load baseline; this also fulfils the slice agent's consumes (RRU.PrbTotDl). Step 2 (slice/monitor) is the read-only slice-state check: it reports reserved capacity per slice to verify the 30% STATIC partition is actually configured/enforced, and UE-to-slice associations so the KPM throughput measurements can be attributed to operator B. RC is excluded because no control decision is applied or validated (audit only), and TC is excluded because the question is radio PRB partitioning, not transport queue treatment. Risks: on the FlexRIC emulator the slice monitor reflects emulated state, and KPM attribution depends on stable UE-to-slice mapping; if reserved capacity deviates from 30%, a follow-up chain (kpm -> slice/apply-static -> kpm) would be the next best action to re-enforce and re-measure.

planner_plan.rationale: Activation-then-verify chain, composed rather than reusing the slice-assurance template unchanged (its slice step is read-only 'monitor', which cannot activate the broadcast-media slice). Step 1 (kpm observe-rru) is required first because the slice agent consumes RRU.PrbTotDl, which only KPM produces; it also captures the pre-activation PRB baseline. Step 2 (slice apply-static) pushes the E2SM-SLICE STATIC control to reserve the marathon slice's fixed PRB share and includes built-in slice monitoring. Step 3 (kpm observe-ue) confirms from live measurements (DRB.UEThpDl, PRB usage, UE-to-slice association) that the camera feeds are actually being carried. RC is deliberately excluded: its card forbids use for slice PRB reservation, and on this emulator its CONTROL-ACK has no effect on later KPIs, so measurement-based confirmation is the correct validation path. Risk: if the final KPM window shows no UE throughput on the slice, the follow-up is to re-run slice apply-static and check UE-to-slice association via slice monitor before escalating.

Next best action: if the reserved share is below the contractual share, or usage is throttled while cell PRBs are free, re-plan with slice/apply-static to raise tenant C's reservation, followed by a kpm re-check to validate the change.

planner_plan.rationale: ECN marking on the default bearer queue is transport active queue management, which is squarely the TC service model's scope; RC is excluded because its card explicitly rules out queue management (it only pushes per-UE E2SM-RC bearer control, acknowledged but ineffective on KPIs in the emulator), and SLICE is irrelevant (no PRB partitioning requested). No operator template matches this exact intent, so the chain is composed from cards. KPM runs first with observe-ue because TC consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, which only KPM produces, and it captures a pre-change queue-delay baseline. TC then runs apply-all (full profile) to enable ECN marking on the bearer queue, with its built-in RLC monitor surfacing RLC.queue_stats for immediate feedback; apply-codel was rejected as it pins the CoDel-only profile. Risks: TC writes target the emulated tc_control resource, so observed KPI movement may be limited; and the chosen action is the closest match since no dedicated ECN-only action exists. Next best action: re-run kpm observe-ue after the change to confirm the queue-delay trend, and only escalate to an RC validation step if a per-UE bearer-side check is later required.

RC is excluded: its card forbids queue-management use, its QoS-flow-to-DRB control is ack-only with no effect on later KPIs on the emulator, and no radio bearer remap is requested. Slice is excluded since no PRB partitioning or slice isolation is in scope. Risk: if TC classification cannot distinguish the update class on the shared path, the 10 Mbit/s cap may not bind; fallback is slice-level capacity partitioning via slice apply-static. Next best action: execute the chain, then diff post-control DRB.RlcSduDelayDl and DRB.UEThpDl against the KPM baseline before considering slice escalation.

rationale.next_best_action: Run kpm(observe-ue) -> tc(apply-all) -> rc(rc-control), then re-run kpm observe-ue to confirm the software-update class holds ~10 Mbit/s and DRB.RlcSduDelayDl for interactive flows recovers; tighten the TC class filter if interactive delay does not improve.
rationale.observations: Intent is a per-class transport rate cap (10 Mbit/s) on the shared bearer path - TC service-model territory (shaping, partitioning, traffic classification), not slice PRB reservation or radio bearer control. TC consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, which only KPM produces, so KPM must precede TC; observe-ue also baselines the crowding evidence (DRB.UEThpDl, RLC SDU delay). Operator history supports TC's write scope here: it was rejected only for a read-only diagnosis intent, while control-applying intents (capacity headroom) accepted TC plus a final RC validation.
rationale.risks: On the FlexRIC emulator RC's control is acknowledged but has no effect on later KPIs, so rc-control confirms the control decision was accepted, not that the cap is enforced - enforcement must be verified by post-checking KPM/RLC stats. apply-all changes treatment on the shared path, so a mis-classified filter could shape interactive flows too. SLICE is deliberately excluded: per-class shaping is not PRB partitioning.

TC is the enforcement point for traffic-class queueing/priority, and this workflow pairs TC actions with bearer/tunnel (GTP) observers for transport-aware feedback. Slice-assurance targets slice policy rather than per-class queueing, and observe-diagnose-optimize adds KPM/SLICE/RC steps not required for a direct QoS enforcement action. planner_plan.rationale: The intent is transport-level per-class treatment (dedicated queue partition for IoT telemetry so it stops queuing behind video), which maps to the TC service model: its card explicitly covers partitioning and traffic classification. Action apply-all is chosen over apply-codel because CoDel-only AQM mitigates bufferbloat but does not create a per-class partition; the full profile includes classification/partitioning plus the RLC monitor. TC consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, which only KPM produces, so KPM must run first — observe-ue is the DRB-oriented action that baselines per-flow queueing delay (IoT vs video) and satisfies the data dependency. RC is excluded: its card forbids use for queue management (TC), and its QoS-flow-to-DRB bearer control cannot express a transport queue partition (and on the emulator is ack-only with no KPI effect). Slice is excluded: STATIC PRB reservation is radio-side capacity partitioning, not transport queueing. Chain is 2 steps, within the 1-4 preference, and matches the operator's accepted KPM->TC pattern for transport queue issues. Risks: TC policy effect is not self-validated, and classification must correctly tag IoT telemetry flows or the partition won't help. Next best action: run the chain, then re-run kpm observe-ue to confirm IoT-flow RLC SDU delay drops while video throughput is unaffected.

planner_plan.rationale: Measure-then-shape chain matching the operator-accepted [KPM, TC, RC] pattern for uplink-latency intents. (1) kpm/observe-ue quantifies the harm first: per-UE RLC SDU delay and throughput show how much the van's large uplink uploads inflate latency for other UEs on the cell, and it supplies DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, which TC consumes. (2) tc/apply-all runs the full TC profile - traffic classification plus shaping of the upload class with CoDel AQM - matching the explicit 'shape the upload class' ask and bounding the uplink queue to stop bufferbloat. (3) rc/rc-control closes the loop by pushing the QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping and awaiting E2 CONTROL-ACK, since RC goes last when a control decision is applied and validated. SLICE is deliberately excluded: PRB reservation is a write scope not required by this intent and was previously rejected as a forbidden writer; the transport-qos-only template was rejected because the intent requires measurement before control. Risks: on the FlexRIC emulator RC control is acknowledged but has no effect on later KPIs, so validation is acknowledgment-only; TC shapes the transport/bearer path, so radio-side uplink scheduling remains a residual bottleneck if PRB stays saturated. Next best action: re-run kpm/observe-ue after apply-all to confirm the delay reduction, and escalate to slice-level PRB partitioning only if uplink congestion persists.

planner_plan.rationale: Confirm-then-fix loop scoped to queue level only. Step 1 (kpm/observe-ue) reads live E2SM-KPM UE/DRB records (DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, DRB.UEThpDl) on cell 5 to confirm the reported ~40 ms jitter; this is exactly the queueing-delay evidence tc consumes. Step 2 (tc/apply-codel) is a conditional edge: execute only if the KPM window shows sustained ~40 ms RLC SDU delay consistent with bufferbloat; CoDel AQM is a queue-level-only remedy, matching the constraint. Step 3 (kpm/observe-ue) re-reads the same KPIs to verify the post-control delta (closed loop). Dependencies hold: tc consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl produced in step 1; kpm has no requires. slice (PRB reservation) and rc (per-UE bearer control) are excluded because the fix must be queue-level only, and rc control is documented as having no effect on later KPIs on this emulator. Observations: all cards are status 'ready' (none deprecated), no conflicts_with entries, all near-RT at 1 s timescale. Risks: (1) if PRB utilisation is saturated the jitter may be scheduler-driven and CoDel only partially helps — within queue-only scope, tc apply-all (shaping/classification + RLC monitor) is the fallback lever; (2) emulator TC changes may show a small KPM delta, so cross-check RLC.queue_stats if the recheck is inconclusive; (3) the KPM subscription window must span the gaming peak to capture the spike. Next best action: run kpm observe-ue on cell 5 now, gate tc apply-codel on confirmed RLC SDU delay >= 40 ms, then re-run kpm observe-ue to confirm jitter reduction.

planner_plan.rationale: Queue-scoped intent: confirm 40 ms jitter on cell 5 from live measurements, then fix only at the queue level. Step 1 (kpm/observe-ue) reads UE/DRB-oriented KPM records and yields DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, the direct evidence of queue-induced jitter; KPM is read-only and is correctly placed first for observation/diagnosis. Step 2 (tc/apply-codel) is the only queue-level writer (CoDel AQM targets bufferbloat/queueing delay) and consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl produced by step 1, satisfying the data dependency; its write scope is explicitly required by the intent, so it does not hit the 'forbidden writer' rejection pattern seen in past proposals. Step 3 repeats kpm/observe-ue as a post-control measurement check (explicitly supported by the KPM card) to verify the spikes subsided, closing the loop adaptively; gate step 2 on step 1 evidence — if RLC SDU delay is normal, skip the TC write. Exclusions: slice is omitted because PRB reservation is not a queue-level fix and the intent says queue only; rc is omitted because it is radio bearer control (its card forbids use for queue management, and its emulator ACK has no effect on KPIs), so the observe-diagnose-optimize template was not reused unchanged; the transport-qos template (TC alone) was rejected because TC's consumed DRB.RlcSduDelayDl would have no upstream provider. Risks: CoDel needs a short settling interval before the verification window; if post-control KPM still shows spikes, the cause is likely beyond the queue (radio/slice) and should be escalated in a follow-up intent rather than widening this chain.

Step 2 tc/apply-all runs the full TC profile (ECN AQM rather than the drop-based CoDel profile) with the RLC monitor for queue stats. Step 3 kpm/observe-ue re-measures to verify the ECN change closed the loop.
rationale.exclusions: RC excluded: its E2SM-RC control is QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping, not queue management, and is acknowledged but ineffective on KPIs in this emulator. Slice excluded: no PRB partitioning or slice isolation requested.
rationale.next_action: Execute kpm observe-ue to snapshot the delay/throughput baseline, trigger tc apply-all to move the telemetry bearer to ECN marking, then re-run observe-ue and compare DRB.RlcSduDelayDl and retransmission-correlated queue stats against the baseline.
rationale.observation: Rising retransmissions on telemetry flows indicate transport queueing loss; baseline DL delay (DRB.RlcSduDelayDl) and throughput (DRB.UEThpDl) must be captured before any policy change.
risks: TC card exposes no dedicated ECN action; apply-all (full profile) is the closest executable match to ECN marking - confirm the profile enables ECN before dispatch.
If delay remains high after ECN, the bottleneck may be radio-side (PRB contention), requiring an observe-rru or slice follow-up.
On the FlexRIC emulator, TC policy effects on downstream KPM may be limited; treat step 3 as confirmation of policy application, not guaranteed KPI improvement.

The queueing change (drop-based -> ECN marking) is transport AQM, squarely the TC agent's scope; apply-codel runs the CoDel profile, the ECN-marking AQM, matching the 'transport-qos' procedure without forcing the broader 4-step template. A closing KPM observe-ue re-check validates delay/throughput after the policy lands (KPM card explicitly supports post-control measurement). RC is excluded: its card says do not use for queue management, its only control is a fixed QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping, and on this emulator its control does not affect later KPIs. Slice is irrelevant (no PRB partitioning requested). Risks: ECN marking only reduces retransmissions if the telemetry senders negotiate ECN-capable TCP; if delay persists, retransmissions may be RLC/air-interface driven rather than queue drops. Next best action: execute the chain, then if DRB.RlcSduDelayDl stays elevated, escalate TC to apply-all (full profile + RLC monitor) for RLC.queue_stats before considering radio-side agents.

planner_plan.rationale: Observation: rising retransmissions on telemetry flows point to transport queue drops, so the chain observes first, then actuates on the transport path. kpm/observe-ue reads the UE/DRB KPIs the intent names - DRB.RlcSduDelayDl (delay) and DRB.UEThpDl (throughput) - and supplies the DRB.RlcSduDelayDl that tc consumes, satisfying the dependency rule. tc/apply-all then runs the full TC profile to move the telemetry bearer from drop-based queueing to ECN marking, and its RLC monitor returns RLC.queue_stats to verify queue behaviour after the switch (apply-codel would keep the drop-based CoDel profile, contradicting the intent). SLICE is excluded: the past 'missing required SLICE' rejection applied to a radio PRB-congestion intent, while transport-queue intents (bufferbloat, video queue buildup) were accepted without it, and ECN marking is queue treatment, not PRB partitioning. RC is excluded: E2SM-RC control is radio bearer/QoS-flow mapping, explicitly not queue management, and on this emulator its CONTROL-ACK has no effect on later KPIs, so it would be a no-op step. Risk: if KPM shows low RLC SDU delay with high PRB utilisation, the cause is radio scheduling rather than queueing and the plan should be replanned toward slice/PRB actions; ECN also only helps if telemetry senders respond to marks (ECN-capable TCP). Next best action: execute kpm then tc, then re-run kpm/observe-ue to confirm delay and retransmissions fall; if ECN marks rise without relief, review the telemetry senders' congestion control.

KPM runs first (observe-rru) to gather fresh RRU.PrbTotDl/PrbTotUl evidence for cell 9 and check whether the 90% PRB reading is sustained or a transient/counter artifact. Slice monitor runs second as a read-only cross-check: it consumes RRU.PrbTotDl from KPM and reports UE-to-slice associations and reserved capacity, corroborating whether observed PRB load is consistent with actual attached-UE demand (genuine congestion) or diverges from it (suspected counter/measurement glitch). No template matches this investigate-only procedure, so a novel 2-step read-only chain was composed. Risk: slice monitor reflects slice-level state, not per-PRB counters, so disagreement is indicative rather than conclusive; a KPM re-poll over a longer window remains the fallback. Next best action: execute the chain, then if evidence confirms genuine load, re-plan with a mitigation chain (e.g., slice apply-static) under operator approval.

Step 1 kpm/observe-rru measures current PRB utilisation to confirm eMBB idling at ~15% and URLLC saturation, and satisfies slice's consumes of RRU.PrbTotDl. Step 2 slice/apply-static applies the STATIC profile shifting PRB reservation from eMBB toward URLLC based on the measured load; the slice suite itself validates the policy and reports UE-to-slice associations and reserved capacity. Step 3 kpm/observe-rru re-measures PRB utilisation to verify the transfer closed the URLLC saturation without starving eMBB. Risks: STATIC profile is a coarse whole-reservation repartition (no per-UE scheduling change, so TC/RC are out of scope); verification window must be long enough to see steady-state utilisation; if eMBB load returns, a follow-up apply-static rebalance is the next best action.

planner_plan.rationale: Two-step observe-then-act chain. (1) kpm/observe-rru first: read-only E2SM-KPM check of current PRB utilisation on the cells covering the drone route; it produces RRU.PrbTotDl, which the slice agent consumes, satisfying the dependency rule. (2) slice/apply-static: reserves PRB for the drones' command-and-control slice via the STATIC profile and validates with its built-in monitor (slice.ue_association, reserved capacity), so it both applies and confirms the control decision. TC excluded (transport/queue policies, not slice PRB); RC excluded (per-UE bearer control, card explicitly forbids use for slice PRB reservation, and apply-static already validates). Risks: STATIC profile is fixed capacity — size the reservation above observed baseline load plus drone C2 demand before the 14:00 flight start; on the FlexRIC emulator, control is acknowledged but downstream KPI effects may be limited, so re-run kpm observe-rru after apply-static to confirm headroom. Next best action: run kpm observe-rru now, review PRB headroom on route cells, then trigger slice apply-static with the C2 reservation sized from the snapshot.

TC consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, which only KPM produces, so KPM (observe-ue, the UE/DRB-oriented read) must run first to satisfy the data dependency and capture a pre-change baseline. Acceptance confirmation is provided by TC's own outputs (tc.policy plus RLC.queue_stats from the built-in monitor) rather than by RC: the RC card explicitly forbids use for TC queue management, its only control action is a fixed QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping (DRB 5, QFI 10) that cannot apply or acknowledge a shaper, and on this emulator its CONTROL-ACK has no real effect. Slice is excluded because no PRB partitioning is requested. Risk: no ready card emits a transport-level control-ack, so 'network accepted' is evidenced by tc.policy/queue stats rather than an E2 ack; if effect validation is also desired, the next best action is to re-run kpm observe-ue after TC and compare DRB.RlcSduDelayDl against the baseline.

planner_plan.rationale: Observations: switching the default bearer AQM from CoDel drops to ECN marking is transport/queue control, so TC is the actuator; RC is excluded because its card explicitly forbids queue management (TC) and notes its control is ACKed with no KPI effect on the emulator. Step 1 (kpm/observe-ue) captures baseline DRB.RlcSduDelayDl queue-delay evidence and supplies the DRB.RlcSduDelayDl input that TC consumes. Step 2 (tc/apply-all) applies the full TC profile with the RLC monitor and emits RLC.queue_stats; apply-codel was rejected because it would re-assert the current drop-based CoDel behavior. Step 3 (kpm/observe-ue) re-reads UE/DRB KPIs to verify the policy change took effect against the baseline. Risks: (1) the TC card exposes no explicit apply-ecn action, so apply-all's full profile must actually select ECN marking or the switch silently no-ops; (2) emulator controls can be ACKed without KPI impact, so verification must compare pre/post KPM deltas and RLC.queue_stats, not just control ACKs. Next best action: execute the chain and diff pre/post DRB.RlcSduDelayDl and RLC.queue_stats; if ECN marking is not reflected in the KPIs, extend the TC card with a dedicated apply-ecn action and re-run.

planner_plan.rationale: TC is the only executable agent that applies CoDel/ECN active queue management, so it owns the control: apply-all runs the full TC profile (ECN marking rather than the CoDel profile) with the RLC monitor, producing tc.policy and RLC.queue_stats as direct evidence of the switch. KPM leads to baseline DRB.RlcSduDelayDl (satisfying TC's declared consumes) and repeats after the control to verify the change went through via delay/queue KPIs. RC is deliberately excluded despite past [TC, RC] acceptances: its card forbids use for queue management, its only control is a fixed QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping unrelated to AQM, and on this emulator its CONTROL-ACK is a no-op, so it would add false confirmation. Slice is out of scope (no PRB partitioning in the intent). Risks: there is no dedicated apply-ecn action, so apply-all's full profile is assumed to carry the ECN marking treatment; KPM is read-only, so verification is inferential from RLC.queue_stats and DRB.RlcSduDelayDl rather than an explicit policy read-back. Next best action: execute the baseline, apply the ECN profile, then the post-check; if RLC.queue_stats still report drops instead of ECN marks, re-run the TC suite with the ECN profile explicitly confirmed before treating the switch as complete.

Step 1 (kpm observe-rru) captures the current post-failure KPI baseline and supplies RRU.PrbTotDl, which the slice agent consumes. Step 2 (slice apply-static) performs the actual rollback: it sends the E2SM-SLICE STATIC profile and monitors slice indications, giving direct evidence the control was accepted (slice.policy, slice.ue_association). Step 3 (kpm observe-rru) is the post-control measurement check confirming the rollback took effect with no KPI regression. RC was deliberately excluded: its E2SM-RC control is per-UE radio bearer mapping, its card explicitly forbids using it for slice PRB reservation, and on this emulator its ACK has no effect on later KPIs, so it adds no validation value. Risk: slice apply-static is a write action on slice_control — if the E2 node rejects the STATIC profile, the final KPM step will still show the pre-rollback state, so compare slice.ue_association and PRB figures against the step-1 baseline. Next best action: execute the chain and verify the step-3 KPM snapshot matches the static-baseline partitioning before closing the incident.

Step 1 (kpm/observe-ue) reads UE/DRB-oriented KPM records including DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, providing the delay evidence that gates the decision; KPM is correctly first per observation rule and is read-only. Step 2 (rc/rc-control) exactly implements the remap: E2SM-RC style 1 Radio Bearer Control, action 2 QoS flow mapping (DRB 5, QFI 10, DL, amf_ue_ngap_id 1) with E2 CONTROL-ACK confirmation; RC is correctly last per actuation rule. TC and SLICE are excluded: their write scopes (transport queue control, slice PRB policy) are not required by this per-UE bearer-mapping intent, matching the operator's prior rejection of unnecessary writers; SLICE also does not handle per-UE QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping. No template matches (observe-diagnose-optimize adds unneeded SLICE/TC), so a novel 2-step chain is composed. Dependencies satisfied: neither agent has unmet requires/consumes, and KPM's delay snapshot feeds the RC gating condition. Next best action: run kpm/observe-ue, evaluate DRB.RlcSduDelayDl against the 50 ms threshold, and trigger rc-control only on breach.

Dependency check passes: both agents have empty requires/consumes. planner_plan.rationale: Observation: the intent needs diagnosis first, so KPM leads with observe-ue to pull per-UE/DRB evidence (DRB.UEThpDl, DRB.RlcSduDelayDl) for the VIP's connection and rule out cell-wide congestion vs. a bearer-specific problem. Fix: if the bearer mapping is at fault, RC runs rc-control last — E2SM-RC style 1 QoS-flow-to-DRB mapping scoped to the single UE (amf_ue_ngap_id 1) — and confirms via E2 CONTROL-ACK, satisfying 'RC last for control/validation'. Exclusions: TC (transport queueing) and SLICE (PRB partitioning) are writers whose scopes are not required by this per-UE bearer intent; past operator rejections flag exactly this as 'forbidden writer', and the observe-diagnose-optimize template is not requested so it is not reused. Risks: on the FlexRIC emulator the RC control is ACKed but has no effect on later KPIs, so do not add a post-control KPM step expecting deltas — treat the ACK plus rc.ue_info (RRC state) as confirmation. Next best action: if observe-ue shows cell-wide PRB saturation instead of a per-UE bearer fault, halt before rc-control and escalate to the operator before any slice/TC change.
